Many compatibilists seem to think that they need only present a conditional analysis of ability, defend it against, or modify it in the face of, such counter-examples as may arise, and that they have thereby done what is necessary to defend compatibilism. That is not how I see it. The particular analysis of ability that a compatibilist presents is, as I see it, simply one of his premisses; his central premiss, in fact. And premisses need to be defended. (van Inwagen 1983, 121)[^inwagen-1983]
zh: 该分析为我们做了什么？它如何影响我们对相容性问题的理解？就我所能见，它几乎帮不了我们什么，除非我们有理由认为它是 ** 正确的 **。许多相容论者似乎认为：他们只需给出一个能力的条件句分析，在可能出现的反例面前为它辩护或修改它，从而就算完成了捍卫相容论所必需的工作。我不这样看。在我看来，相容论者给出的那个具体能力分析，不过是他的一个前提——实际上是其中心前提。而前提是需要辩护的。（van Inwagen 1983, 121）[^inwagen-1983]

en: van Inwagen’s point is that, provided the incompatibilist has offered *arguments* for the claim that such abilities are incompatible with determinism—as, in van Inwagen’s presentation, the incompatibilist has—the production of an analysis is as yet no answer to those arguments. For those arguments are also arguments, *inter alia*, against the compatibilist’s favored account of ability.
zh: van Inwagen 的要点是：只要不相容论者已经为“此类能力与决定论不相容”这一主张提供了 ** 论证 **——按 van Inwagen 的呈现，不相容论者已经提供了——那么给出一个分析尚不构成对这些论证的回应。因为那些论证除其他外，恰恰也是针对相容论者中意的那种能力说明的论证。

en: There are, then, at least two obstacles for the compatibilist who wishes to appeal to an account of ability in defense of compatibilism. First, there is the general difficulty of actually giving an extensionally adequate theory of ability. Now there is also van Inwagen’s point just outlined, namely that arguments for the incompatibility of abilities and determinism are, *inter alia*, arguments against any theory of ability that is congenial to the compatibilist. Taken together, these points seem to pose a serious obstacle to any theory of ability that is both compatible with determinism and in accord with our ordinary judgments about what ability requires.
zh: 于是，想诉诸能力说明来捍卫相容论的相容论者至少面临两个障碍。第一，实际给出一个外延得当的能力理论这一普遍困难。其次则是 van Inwagen 刚才指出的要点：能力与决定论不相容的论证，除其他外，也是针对任何让相容论者顺心的能力理论的论证。合起来，这些要点似乎对任何既与决定论相容、又合乎我们关于能力之要求的日常判断的能力理论构成严重障碍。

en: One response is to make a distinction between two kinds of compatibilist project. (Compare Pryor 2000 on responses to skepticism)[^pryor-2000]. One project is to *convince* someone moved by the incompatibilist’s arguments to retreat from her position. Call this *ambitious* compatibilism. For precisely the reasons van Inwagen gives, it is doubtful that any theory of ability will suffice for a defense of ambitious compatibilism. There is another project, however, that the compatibilist might be engaging in. Let us say that, for some reason or other, she herself is not convinced by the incompatibilist’s argument. She is still left with an explanatory burden, namely to explain, if only to her *own* satisfaction, how it *could be* that abilities are compatible with the truth of determinism. Here the compatibilist’s aim is not to convince the incompatibilist of the error of her ways, but simply to work out a satisfactory conception of compatibilism. Let us call this *modest* compatibilism. This distinction is not often made, and it is not always clear which of these projects classical compatibilists are engaged in. If the latter project is indeed part of classical compatibilism, then we may grant many of the above points while still granting the theory of ability a central place in defenses of compatibilism. For it may be that, though a theory of ability is of no use to the ambitious compatibilist, it has a crucial role to play in the defense of modest compatibilism about freedom and determinism.
zh: 一种回应是区分两种相容论工程（比较 Pryor 2000 对怀疑论回应的区分）[^pryor-2000]。一个工程是 ** 说服 ** 被不相容论者论证打动的人放弃其立场。称之为 ** 进取的 ** （ambitious）相容论。恰恰由于 van Inwagen 给出的理由，任何能力理论是否足以捍卫进取的相容论，是可疑的。然而相容论者还可能在从事另一个工程。让我们说，出于这样那样的原因，她本人并未被不相容论者的论证说服。她仍背负一种说明负担：即便只为自己 ** 满意 **，也要解释能力 ** 如何可能 ** 与决定论的真相容。这里相容论者的目标不是让不相容论者改宗，而只是推出一个令人满意的相容论概念。让我们称之为 ** 谦抑的 ** （modest）相容论。这一区分并不常被做出，而且经典相容论者从事的是哪个工程并不总是清楚。如果后一工程确实是经典相容论的一部分，那么我们可以承认上述许多要点，同时仍承认能力理论在相容论辩护中的核心地位。因为可能的情况是：能力理论对进取的相容论者无用，却在关于自由与决定论的谦抑相容论的辩护中扮演关键角色。

en: Finally, in addition to bearing on questions about freedom and determinism, a theory of ability can be expected to have something to say about another issue central to the free will debates, namely the metaphysical conditions on moral responsibility. Consider so-called ‘Frankfurt cases’. These are cases due to Frankfurt (1969), where an agent chooses to and performs some action *A* while at the same time there is some other action *B* such that, had the agent been about to choose *B*, an ‘intervener’ would have altered the agent’s brain so that the agent would have chosen, and performed, *A* instead. One question about such cases is whether the agent, in the actual sequence of events, had the ability to *B*. Frankfurt’s intuition, and that of most others, is that she did not. Given the further claim that the agent is nonetheless morally responsible for doing *A*, this case appears to be a counterexample to what Frankfurt calls the Principle of Alternative Possibilities (PAP): an agent is morally responsible for *A*ing only if she had the ability to perform some action other than *A*.
zh: 最后，除与自由和决定论的问题相关外，能力理论还可望对自由意志论辩中另一个核心问题——道德责任的形而上学条件——有所言说。考虑所谓的“法兰克福案例”（Frankfurt cases）。这类案例源自 Frankfurt（1969）：行动者选择并实施某行动 *A*，而与此同时存在另一行动 *B*，若行动者即将选择 *B*，一位“干预者”就会改动其大脑，使行动者转而选择并实施 *A*。关于此类案例的一个问题是：在实际的事件序列中，行动者是否拥有实施 *B* 的能力。Frankfurt 的直觉——也是多数人的直觉——是她没有。再加上“行动者仍对实施 *A* 负有道德责任”这一主张，此案例似乎反驳了 Frankfurt 所称的其他可能性原则（Principle of Alternative Possibilities，PAP）：行动者对实施 *A* 负有道德责任，仅当她曾拥有实施 *A* 以外某行动的能力。

en: In recent years, several philosophers — notably the new dispositionalists such as Smith (2003), Vihvelin (2004, 2013), and Fara (2008) — have advocated revisiting our judgments about such cases in light of the theory of ability. As noted in Section 3.4, these authors suggest that the ability to do otherwise should be understood dispositionally, as something that persists even in the presence of certain counterfactual interveners. When applied to a Frankfurt case, this view seems to imply that the agent in question does have the ability to do otherwise after all. We might restate the question raised by these discussions as follows: should ‘ability’ in (PAP) be understood as general ability, or specific ability? If general ability is what matters, then Frankfurt cases may indeed not tell against (PAP), for the agent retains the general ability to do otherwise. If it is specific ability that matters, however, the challenge to (PAP) stands (see also Whittle 2010)[^whittle-2010]. This is a vital question for understanding the purported connection between ability and questions of moral responsibility, whichever theory of ability we accept.
zh: 近年来，好几位哲学家——尤其是新倾向主义者如 Smith（2003）、Vihvelin（2004, 2013）与 Fara（2008）——主张依据能力理论重审我们对此类案例的判断。如第 3.4 节所述，这些作者提出，“另做他事”的能力应作倾向式理解：即使某些反事实干预者在场，它依然持续。应用于法兰克福案例时，这一看法似乎蕴含：所论行动者终究拥有另做他事的能力。我们可以把这些讨论提出的问题重述为：(PAP) 中的“能力”应理解为一般能力还是特定能力？如果重要的是一般能力，那么法兰克福案例确实可能不构成对 (PAP) 的反驳，因为行动者保有另做他事的一般能力。但如果重要的是特定能力，对 (PAP) 的挑战依然成立（另见 Whittle 2010）[^whittle-2010]。无论我们接受哪种能力理论，这对理解能力与道德责任问题之间所谓联系都是一个关键问题。

en: 5.2 Ability and disability
zh: 5.2 能力与残疾

en: An altogether different yet equally important area in which theories of ability may be thought to take on an explanatory role is the philosophy of disability. In particular, some authors propose that to have a disability just is to lack some ability or set of abilities. Let us call this the *ability-based* view of disability. If the ability-based view is correct, then developing an accurate theory of abilities should help us gain a better understanding of disability too. As it turns out, several complex issues arise in trying to make this view precise.
zh: 一个全然不同却同样重要的领域是残疾哲学：能力理论在其中或许被认为承担解释角色。具体而言，一些作者提出：拥有残疾，恰恰就是缺乏某种能力或某组能力。让我们称之为残疾的 ** 基于能力 ** （ability-based）的看法。如果基于能力的看法是对的，那么发展一套准确的能力理论应当也有助于我们更好地理解残疾。事实证明，要把这一看法精确化，会遇到若干复杂问题。

en: To begin with, proponents of ability-based views disagree on the abilities that matter when it comes to disability. On the one hand, there are views with a central naturalistic component, which take the relevant abilities to be determined by a species norm. On these views, to be disabled is to lack an ability to do things that individuals in one’s reference class (e.g., human adults) are ordinarily able to do (Buchanan et al. 2000, p. 286; see also Boorse 2010)[^boorse-2010][^buchanan-2000]. Thus, a person who is deaf is disabled on this view because they lack the ability to hear other people’s voices, which is something that most others in their reference class are able to do. On the other hand, there are evaluative views, which take the abilities that are relevant to disability to be determined by some political, ethical, or social criterion. For example, one might hold that the abilities that matter when determining whether someone is disabled are those we are entitled to as a matter of justice (Begon 2023)[^begon-2023], those that are important for well-being (Nussbaum 2006)[^nussbaum-2006], or those we are socially expected to have (Jenkins and Webster 2021)[^jenkins-2021]. Whether a deaf person is disabled depends, on these views, on whether they lack abilities that are relevant given the view’s preferred social or political criterion.
zh: 首先，基于能力的看法的拥护者对“哪些能力关乎残疾”意见不一。一方面，有些看法带有中心的自然主义成分，认为相关能力由物种规范（species norm）决定。按这些看法，残疾就是缺乏做这样一些事的能力——那些一个人的参照类（如人类成年人）通常能做的事（Buchanan et al. 2000, p. 286；另见 Boorse 2010）[^boorse-2010][^buchanan-2000]。于是，按这种看法，一个失聪者是残疾的，因为他们缺乏听到他人嗓音的能力，而这参照类中的大多数人都做得到。另一方面，还有评价性的看法，认为关乎残疾的能力由某种政治的、伦理的或社会的判准决定。例如，有人可以主张：判断某人是否残疾时相关的能力，是我们出于正义有权拥有的那些能力（Begon 2023）[^begon-2023]、对福祉重要的那些能力（Nussbaum 2006）[^nussbaum-2006]、或社会期望我们拥有的那些能力（Jenkins and Webster 2021）[^jenkins-2021]。按这些看法，一个失聪者是否残疾，取决于他们是否缺乏按该看法偏好的社会或政治判准而言相关的能力。

en: It bears emphasizing that the distinction between naturalistic and evaluative ability-based views is not as neat as the above passage may seem to suggest. Some authors combine elements of each approach. For instance, one might hold that only the lack of some subset of species-normal abilities is relevant to disability. Which subset is relevant may then be determined by political or social concerns.
zh: 值得强调的是，自然主义与评价性基于能力看法之分，并不如上文段落看似的那样整齐。一些作者结合两种进路的要素。例如，有人可以主张：只有物种常规能力的某个子集之缺乏才关乎残疾；而哪一子集相关，又可由政治或社会关切决定。

en: Both naturalistic and evaluative approaches have been challenged. Here, we will focus on two challenges for ability-based view of disability more generally. The first challenge, raised by Elizabeth Barnes (2016), is that there are various conditions that we consider to be disabilities but that do not clearly result in a lack of ability. Take, for instance, fibromyalgia, a condition that tends to manifest as fatigue and chronic pain. On first sight, it is not obvious which abilities a person with this condition lacks. In response, some have suggested that there *is* a clear set of abilities that a person with this condition lacks if we consider abilities to perform temporally extended actions. Both fatigue and chronic pain may interfere with one’s ability to work a 40-hour week, for instance (see Gregory 2020)[^gregory-2020].
zh: 自然主义与评价性两种进路都受到了挑战。这里我们聚焦针对整个基于能力残疾观的两个挑战。第一个挑战由 Elizabeth Barnes（2016）提出：我们视为残疾的各种状况，并不都清楚地导致能力缺乏。以纤维肌痛为例——一种通常表现为疲劳与慢性疼痛的状况。乍看之下，患此症者缺乏哪些能力并不明显。作为回应，有人提出：如果我们考虑实施时间上延展之行动的能力，那么确实存在一组该症患者清楚缺乏的能力。例如，疲劳与慢性疼痛都可能干扰一个人每周工作 40 小时的能力（见 Gregory 2020）[^gregory-2020]。

en: A second challenge arises on the common assumption that having abilities is valuable. If abilities are valuable, and disability *just is* a lack of abilities, this would seem to imply that disability is a “bad difference” (Barnes 2016)[^barnes-2016]. That claim conflicts with the judgments of many members of the Disability Pride Movement, who perceive disability as something to be celebrated rather than as a negative form of bodily difference or a special type of disadvantage. There are several ways in which proponents of an ability-based view might respond to this worry. Firstly, some authors simply insist that disability is a ‘bad difference’. In fact, they argue, this observation helps justify spending resources on accommodations for disabled people. Secondly, some proponents of evaluative views claim that lacking socially expected abilities does not by definition make one worse off, even if it does put one at risk of marginalization (Jenkins and Webster 2021)[^jenkins-2021]. Defining disability as a lack of socially expected abilities may thus be thought to be compatible with the Disability Pride Movement’s celebration of bodily difference. Finally, one might accept that having abilities is valuable, yet reject the idea that having *more* abilities is always preferable. If having more abilities isn’t always good, then lacking some abilities isn’t always bad.
zh: 第二个挑战源自“拥有能力是有价值的”这一常见假定。如果能力有价值，而残疾 ** 恰恰就是 ** 能力之缺乏，这似乎蕴含：残疾是一种“坏差异”（bad difference）（Barnes 2016）[^barnes-2016]。这一主张与残障骄傲运动（Disability Pride Movement）许多成员的判断冲突，后者把残疾看作值得庆祝的东西，而非身体差异的负面形式或一种特殊类型的不利。基于能力看法的拥护者可以用几种方式回应这一担忧。第一，一些作者干脆坚持残疾就是“坏差异”；事实上他们论证，这一观察有助于为投入资源为难障者提供便利提供辩护。第二，评价性看法的一些拥护者主张，缺乏社会期望的能力并不按定义使人境况更糟，即使它确实使人面临边缘化风险（Jenkins and Webster 2021）[^jenkins-2021]。把残疾定义为社会期望能力之缺乏，因而可以被认为与残障骄傲运动对身体差异的庆祝相容。最后，人们可以承认拥有能力有价值，但拒绝“拥有 ** 更多 ** 能力总是更可取”的想法。如果拥有更多能力并不总是好事，那么缺乏一些能力也就并不总是坏事。

en: Abraham Ibn Daud
zh: 亚伯拉罕·伊本·达乌德 Ibn Daud, Abraham (Resianne Fontaine and Amira Eran)

en: **First published Sat Aug 26, 2006; substantive revision Tue Sep 10, 2024**
zh: ** 首次发表于 2006 年 8 月 26 日；2024 年 9 月 10 日实质修订。**

en: Abraham ibn Daud (c.1110–1180) can be regarded as a pioneer in Jewish philosophy. His philosophical treatise *ha-Emunah ha-Ramah* (*The Exalted Faith*, c. 1160) constitutes the first systematic attempt to integrate Aristotelianism into Jewish thought. However, only a few decades later Moses Maimonides, the medieval Jewish philosopher *par excellence*, wrote his philosophical *magnum opus*, *Moreh Nevukhim* (The Guide of the Perplexed), a work that has much in common with Ibn Daud’s book. As a result, *ha-Emunah ha-Ramah* was soon superseded. However, traces of its influence are visible in later medieval Jewish thought. This article will survey Ibn Daud’s major ideas and examine his contribution to medieval Jewish philosophy.
zh: 亚伯拉罕·伊本·达乌德（Abraham ibn Daud，约 1110–1180）可以视为犹太哲学的先驱。他的哲学论著《崇高的信仰》（*ha-Emunah ha-Ramah*，*The Exalted Faith*，约 1160 年）是把亚里士多德主义整合进犹太思想的第一次系统尝试。然而仅仅几十年后，中世纪犹太哲学家中的翘楚摩西·迈蒙尼德写出了他的哲学代表作《迷途指津》（*Moreh Nevukhim*，*The Guide of the Perplexed*），这部著作与伊本·达乌德的书多有相通之处。结果，《崇高的信仰》很快被取而代之。不过，其影响的痕迹在中世纪后期犹太思想中仍清晰可见。本文将综述伊本·达乌德的主要思想，并考察他对中世纪犹太哲学的贡献。

en: 1. Introduction
zh: 1 引言

en: In the introduction to *ha-Emunah ha-Ramah* (henceforth: *ER*) Abraham Ibn Daud states that he decided to write his book in order to solve the problem of free will. Scripture fails to provide an unequivocal answer to this problem since biblical verses on this issue seem to contradict one another. Ibn Daud is convinced that philosophy can help to distinguish between the verses that should be understood literally and those that are in need of interpretation. In his view, the problem in his day is that those who have begun to study philosophy are unable to keep the lamps of philosophy and religion burning simultaneously “for if the lamp of philosophy is kindled, the lamp of religion goes out” (*ER* Eran 2019 104, #6; Samuelson 1986 40 3b–4b)[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]. This is why certain people believe that it is better to steer well clear of the study of philosophy. The consequence is that many Jews are at a loss when it comes to solving religious problems, such as the problem of free will. According to Ibn Daud, this is because they fail to investigate the principles of religion with the help of philosophy and to search for harmony between the two modes of knowledge. His book intends to remedy this situation by showing beginning students of philosophy how to establish such harmony.
zh: 在《崇高的信仰》（下文简称 *ER*）的导言中，亚伯拉罕·伊本·达乌德自陈写作此书是为了解决自由意志问题。经文未能对这一问题给出明确的回答，因为圣经中论及此事的经文似乎彼此矛盾。伊本·达乌德确信，哲学有助于区分哪些经文应按字面理解、哪些需要解释。在他看来，当时的问题在于：已经开始研究哲学的人无法让哲学之灯与宗教之灯同时长明，“因为哲学之灯一旦点燃，宗教之灯就熄灭了”（*ER*，Eran 2019 104, #6；Samuelson 1986 40 3b–4b）[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]。正因如此，有些人认为最好远远避开哲学研究。其后果是，许多犹太人在面对宗教问题——例如自由意志问题——时束手无策。按伊本·达乌德的说法，这是因为他们未能借助哲学来探究宗教诸原理，并在两种知识形态之间寻求和谐。他的书就是要通过向哲学初学者示范如何建立这种和谐来补救这种局面。

en: Ibn Daud thus reveals himself to be a staunch advocate of the study of philosophy and the use of reason to achieve the correct interpretation of problematical biblical passages. In his view, the fact that man is endowed with reason obliges him to use his intellect. Throughout his treatise, he strives to demonstrate how reason and Scripture are not at variance with each other and that “true philosophy” is contained in Scripture.
zh: 伊本·达乌德由此表明自己是哲学研究以及运用理性来正确解读疑难经文的坚定拥护者。在他看来，人被赋予理性这一事实就使人有义务运用其理智。在整部论著中，他力图表明理性与圣经并不相悖，而且“真正的哲学”就包含在圣经之中。

en: 2. Biography
zh: 2 生平

en: The exact date of Ibn Daud’s birth is unknown. It is commonly assumed that he was born c. 1110 in one of the major centers of Muslim Spain, perhaps Cordoba. He himself asserts that he received his education from his maternal uncle, an uncle who is known to have been active as both a teacher and a communal leader in Cordoba, where he died in 1126. Although no further data are available, it is evident from his works that this education must have been a combination of “Greek wisdom” and traditional Jewish learning. Greek wisdom in the cultural setting of Andalusia refers to the study of classical science and philosophy as taught by Muslim scholars and philosophers. Indeed, his writings testify to a thorough familiarity with Greek philosophy and science as read by the Muslim philosophers al-Farabi and Ibn Sina, as well as with rabbinic literature, Hebrew poetry, and Jewish philosophy. He also appears to have had some knowledge of the New Testament and Christian and Muslim polemical literature. Later in life, Ibn Daud moved to Toledo, presumably as a result of the Almohad invasion of Andalusia (1147), an event that led many Jews to flee from Southern Spain. In any event, it is in Toledo that he wrote his two major works in defense of Judaism (circa 1160/61): the philosophical treatise *ER* and the historical *Sefer ha-Qabbalah* (cf. below section 3). Ibn Daud is reported to have died a martyr’s death in Toledo c. 1180. The earliest reference to this was made by the Toledan philosophic author Judah ben Solomon ha-Kohen in his encyclopedia *Midrash ha-Hokhmah* (first half of the 13ᵗʰ century).
zh: 伊本·达乌德的确切生年不详。通常认为他约于 1110 年生于穆斯林西班牙的某一大中心，或许是科尔多瓦。他自述其教育得自舅父；这位舅父以教师与社团领袖的双重身份活跃于科尔多瓦，卒于 1126 年。虽然别无更多材料，但从其著作可以明显看出，这种教育必定是“希腊智慧”与传统犹太学问的结合。在安达卢西亚的文化语境中，“希腊智慧”指穆斯林学者与哲学家所传授的古典科学与哲学之研习。的确，其著作证明他精熟于穆斯林哲学家法拉比与伊本·西那所读的希腊哲学与科学，同样也精熟于拉比文献、希伯来诗歌与犹太哲学。他似乎还对《新约》以及基督教与穆斯林的论战文献有所了解。晚年伊本·达乌德迁居托莱多，其原因很可能是穆瓦希德王朝入侵安达卢西亚（1147 年）——该事件使许多犹太人逃离西班牙南部。无论如何，正是在托莱多，他写成了捍卫犹太教的两大著作（约 1160/61 年）：哲学论著 *ER* 与史学著作《传统之书》（*Sefer ha-Qabbalah*）（参见下文第 3 节）。据载，伊本·达乌德约于 1180 年在托莱多殉道而死。关于此事最早的记载出自托莱多的哲学作家犹大·本·所罗门·哈科恩，见于其百科全书《智慧米德拉什》（*Midrash ha-Hokhmah*，十三世纪上半叶）。

en: Since 1954 scholars of Jewish and Latin philosophy have been intrigued by M.T. d’Alverny’s suggestion that Abraham Ibn Daud is the same person as the twelfth-century Arabic-into-Latin translator Avendauth, also known as “Avendeuth philosophus israelita”, who collaborated with Dominicus Gundissalinus in Toledo. Recent studies on the Toledan Arabic-into-Latin translation program have provided strong support in favor of d’Alverny’s identity suggestion. These new studies portray Avendauth as the motive force (Bertolacci 2011:54)[^bertolacci-2011] behind the Latin translations of Ibn Sina (D’Alverny 1954; Bertolacci 2011; Burnett 2009; Fidora 2011; Hasse 2006; Schwartz 2013; Freudenthal 2016; .
zh: 自 1954 年以来，犹太哲学与拉丁哲学的研究者一直对 M.T. 达尔韦尼的猜想兴趣不减：亚伯拉罕·伊本·达乌德与十二世纪的阿拉伯-拉丁翻译家阿文道特（Avendauth，亦称“Avendeuth philosophus israelita”）是同一人，后者曾在托莱多与多米尼库斯·贡迪萨利努斯合作。关于托莱多阿拉伯-拉丁翻译计划的近期研究，为达尔韦尼的同一性猜想提供了有力支持。这些新研究把阿文道特描绘为伊本·西那著作拉丁翻译背后的推动力（Bertolacci 2011:54）[^bertolacci-2011]（DʼAlverny 1954; Bertolacci 2011; Burnett 2009; Fidora 2011; Hasse 2006; Schwartz 2013; Freudenthal 2016）。

en: In addition to their collaboration as translators, Gundissalinus and Ibn Daud also wrote books of their own. They often used materials from their translated books for their independent books and used parallel arguments to defend their (frequently conflicting) points of view. They both aimed in their own writings to simplify complicated theological and philosophical matters and demonstrated an impressive acquaintance with Ibn Gabirol and Ibn Sina.
zh: 除合作翻译之外，贡迪萨利努斯与伊本·达乌德也各有著述。他们常把自己译书中的材料用于各自的独立著作，并以平行的论证来捍卫他们（时常相互冲突）的观点。二人在自己的写作中都力求简化繁难的神学与哲学问题，并且都对伊本·盖比鲁勒与伊本·西那表现出令人惊叹的熟稔。

en: 3. Major Works
zh: 3 主要著作

en: Ibn Daud’s two major works are *Sefer ha-Qabbalah* (The Book of Tradition) and *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah*. Both books were written around the same time (c. 1160). They are closely related in the sense that they endeavor to defend rabbinic Judaism; the former with the help of history and the latter with the help of philosophy.
zh: 伊本·达乌德的两大著作是《传统之书》（*Sefer ha-Qabbalah*，*The Book of Tradition*）与《崇高的信仰》。两书写作时间相近（约 1160 年），且关系密切：都致力于捍卫拉比犹太教——前者借助历史，后者借助哲学。

en: The purpose of *Sefer ha-Emunah ha-Ramah* was to prove the truth of the words of the prophets by philosophical means, while *Sefer ha-Qabbalah* and related historical works were intended to confirm the validity of the prophecies by demonstrating the reliability of their transmission from one generation to the next
zh: 《崇高的信仰》的目的在于以哲学手段证明先知之言的真理，而《传统之书》及相关史学著作则意在通过展示预言在代际传承中的可靠性来确证预言的有效性。

en: In *Sefer ha-Qabbalah*, which has become a classic in Hebrew literature, Abraham ibn Daud provides a survey of Jewish and general history and attempts to demonstrate the continuity of rabbinic Judaism. According to G.D.Cohen this work also conveys an esoteric message of messianic redemption, a thesis that was challenged by E. Krakowski (2007) as well as by K. Vehlow, who also edited the two chronicles appended to *Sefer ha-Qabbalah*: one on the history of the kings of Israel during the Second Temple period, and the other on the history of Rome, which are similarly polemical (2013). The chronicles had a wide impact on Protestant authors from the 16th century onwards. According to Krakowski, *Sefer ha-Qabbalah* did not convey a coded message for salvation in 1189. Furthermore, Vehlow (2016) and more recently, José Antonio Fernández López (2019, 2023) emphasize the political-polemical message of consolation in *Sefer ha-Qabbalah.*
zh: 在已成为希伯来文学经典的《传统之书》中，亚伯拉罕·伊本·达乌德概述了犹太史与通史，并力图证明拉比犹太教的连续性。按 G.D. 科恩的看法，此书还传达了弥赛亚救赎的隐微讯息；这一论点受到 E. 克拉科夫斯基（2007）与 K. 韦洛的质疑，后者还编辑了附于《传统之书》的两部编年史：其一记第二圣殿时期以色列诸王的历史，另一部记罗马史，二者同样具有论战性质（2013）。这些编年史自十六世纪起对新教作家有广泛影响。按克拉科夫斯基的看法，《传统之书》并没有传达什么 1189 年得救的密码讯息。此外，韦洛（2016）以及晚近的何塞·安东尼奥·费尔南德斯·洛佩斯（2019, 2023）则强调《传统之书》中政治-论战性的抚慰讯息。

en: While the *Book of Tradition* provides a comprehensive narrative of Jewish history, the other three following sections – known as *Dorot ‘Olam* – describe specific aspects or periods in the nation’s life. The *Chronicle of Rome* (*Zikhron Divrey Romi*) locates Spain in a broad Christian context. Ibn Daud picks crucial cases that appear as significant factors in the history of the early church to form an overall polemical argument against Christianity. *The History of the Kings of Israel* (*Divrey Malkhey Yisra’el*), which leans heavily on *Sefer Josippon* (*Book of Josippon*), focuses on the history of the Second Temple Period, from Alexander the Great to the battle of Masada. The last section, *Midrash on Zechariah*, uses the redemptive promises of Zechariah 11, to express Ibn Daud’s national vision. The main theme of Ibn Daud’s historiographical writings, inspired by the cultural atmosphere of Toledo and the Iberian Peninsula in the twelfth century is religious-political authority. Ibn Daud attacks the reliability of the New Testament as part of his wider effort to prove that the superiority of the chosen Jewish community, led by a continuous chain of selected persons over generations is documented in an irrefutable transmitted text. *Dorot ‘Olam* was first printed in Mantua in the early 16th century, in a collection of historical texts entitled *SederʿOlam Rabba* (Greater Order of the World), and became extremely popular among Jewish and Christian Hebraist readers.
zh: 《传统之书》提供了犹太史的全景叙事，而紧随其后的三节——合称《世代之书》（*Dorot ʼOlam*）——描述这个民族的特定方面或时期。《罗马史事记》（*Zikhron Divrey Romi*）把西班牙置于一个宽泛的基督教语境中。伊本·达乌德拣选早期教会历史中看似重要因素的关键案例，构成一个针对基督教的总体论战论证。《以色列诸王史》（*Divrey Malkhey Yisraʼel*）大量倚重《约西蓬书》（*Sefer Josippon*，*Book of Josippon*），聚焦于从亚历山大大帝到马萨达之战的第二圣殿时期历史。最后一节《撒迦利亚米德拉什》则利用《撒迦利亚书》第 11 章的救赎应许来表达伊本·达乌德的民族愿景。伊本·达乌德史学著作的主旨——其灵感来自十二世纪托莱多与伊比利亚半岛的文化氛围——是宗教-政治权威。伊本·达乌德攻击《新约》的可靠性，这是他更宏大努力的一部分：证明由历代拣选者的连续链条所引领的选民共同体的优越性，记载于一部无可辩驳的传承文本之中。《世代之书》于十六世纪初首次印行于曼托瓦，收录于一部题为《大世界之序》（*SederʿOlam Rabba*）的史学文集，并在犹太与基督教希伯来学读者中广为流行。

en: His philosophical book was written in Arabic and entitled *al-‘Aqîdah al-rafî‘ah* (*The Exalted Faith*). The Arabic original is no longer extant. Towards the end of the fourteenth century, the work was translated into Hebrew twice: the first time under the title *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah* by Solomon ben Lavi (c. 1370?), possibly at the instigation of the philosopher Hasdai Crescas, and a second time under the title *Ha-Emunah Nissa’ah* by Samuel ibn Maṭūt. This second translation is based on the first but is less accurate (Eran 1996)[^eran-1996]. Of this version, only one copy is extant, whereas of *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah* 16 manuscripts are known (some of them are not complete).
zh: 他的哲学著作以阿拉伯语写成，题为 *al-ʼAqîdah al-rafîʼah*（《崇高的信仰》）。阿拉伯语原本已佚。十四世纪末，此作两度被译为希伯来语：第一次由所罗门·本·拉维（约 1370 年？）译出，题名 *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah*，或许是在哲学家哈斯代·克雷斯卡斯的推动之下；第二次由撒母耳·伊本·马图特译出，题名 *Ha-Emunah Nissaʼah*。第二个译本以第一个为据，但较不准确（Eran 1996）[^eran-1996]。后一版本仅存一册抄本，而 *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah* 则有 16 种抄本传世（其中若干并不完整）。

en: Ibn Daud is also reported to have written a book on astronomy, the contents of which are unknown. The same applies to an anti-Karaite polemical work, which he mentions himself. Moreover, K. Szilágyi has discovered a fragment of an otherwise unknown work by Ibn Daud on *Physics* in Arabic.
zh: 据载伊本·达乌德还写过一部天文学著作，内容不详。一部反卡拉派的论战著作同样如此，那是他自己提到的。此外，K. 奇拉吉发现了伊本·达乌德一部阿拉伯语《物理学》著作的残篇，此作此前不为人知。

en: In the introduction to *ER*, Ibn Daud mentions two earlier Jewish philosophers: Saadya (often described as the first Jewish philosopher, first half of the 10ᵗʰ century, Baghdad) and the philosopher-poet Solomon ibn Gabirol (11ᵗʰ century, Spain). However, he dismisses their writings claiming that they are inadequate concerning his goal, namely the study of philosophy in order to examine the principles of religion. This statement reflects Ibn Daud’s awareness of introducing a new trend to Jewish philosophy. Saadya’s *Sefer ha-Emunot we-ha-De‘ot* (Book of Opinions and Beliefs) provides a rationalistic interpretation of Judaism but is influenced by the thought of the Muslim kalâm-theologians, which was considered outdated in Ibn Daud’s day, whereas Ibn Gabirol’s *Meqor Hayyim* (known in Latin as *Fons* *Vitae*) is a neo-Platonist work, which does not refer at all to Jewish sources. Indeed, Ibn Daud’s book constitutes a novelty in that it is the first attempt to systematically introduce the Aristotelianism of the Muslim philosophers Alfarabi (870–950) and Ibn Sina (980–1037) into Jewish philosophy. His philosophical terminology and syllogistic reasoning are derived from the works of these authors. His “technical” approach has led Husik to observe that “Ibn Daud leaves upon us the impression of a precise thinker, cold and analytical. He exhibits no grace of style, eloquence of diction or depths of enthusiasm and emotion” (Husik 2002: 198)[^husik-2002]. This judgment of his style may be too harsh. Undoubtedly his book must have made some demands on it readers, but it is only fair to note that Ibn Daud attempts to liven up the monotony of his logical arguments at regular intervals by using analogies and quotes from poems.
zh: 在 *ER* 的导言中，伊本·达乌德提到两位更早的犹太哲学家：萨阿迪亚（常被描述为第一位犹太哲学家，十世纪上半叶，巴格达）与哲学家兼诗人所罗门·伊本·盖比鲁勒（十一世纪，西班牙）。但他对二人的著述并不满意，声称它们就其目标——研习哲学以考察宗教诸原理——而言是不够的。这一表述反映出伊本·达乌德意识到自己正在为犹太哲学引入一种新潮流。萨阿迪亚的《意见与信仰之书》（*Sefer ha-Emunot we-ha-Deʼot*）为犹太教提供了理性主义解释，却受制于穆斯林凯拉姆教义学家的思想，而这在伊本·达乌德的时代已显过时；伊本·盖比鲁勒的《生命之源》（*Meqor Hayyim*，拉丁文称 *Fons Vitae*）则是一部新柏拉图主义著作，全然不涉及犹太文献。的确，伊本·达乌德的书是一项开创之举：它第一次尝试把穆斯林哲学家法拉比（870–950）与伊本·西那（980–1037）的亚里士多德主义系统地引入犹太哲学。他的哲学术语与三段论推理都取自这两位作者的著作。他这种“技术性”的进路使胡西克评曰：“伊本·达乌德给我们留下的印象是一位精确的思想家，冷静而善于分析。他没有风格的优雅、辞令的雄辩，也没有热情与情感的深度”（Husik 2002: 198）[^husik-2002]。对他文风的这一评判或许过于苛刻。无疑，他的书对读者是有要求的；但同样公允的是，伊本·达乌德会定期以类比和诗歌引文来为他那单调的逻辑论证增添生气。

en: 4. Structure and Sources of *ER*
zh: 4 *ER* 的结构与来源

en: 4.1 Structure
zh: 4.1 结构

en: Ibn Daud’s book consists of an introduction and three parts of unequal length. In the introduction, Ibn Daud states that the problem of free will, which prompted him to write his book, can only be solved after the preparatory philosophical study of a variety of issues in the field of physics and metaphysics. In what may be called a “table of contents”, he specifies the various topics to be discussed in his book in his introduction; topics with which the beginning student must become familiar. The first part (Eran 2019 113–357)[^eran-2019] discusses the basic principles of (Aristotelian) physics and metaphysics. It opens with a logical section that treats substance and the categories (I.1). This is followed by discussions on matter, form and the elements (I.2), motion and infinity (I.3–5), the soul (I.6–7) and the heavenly spheres (I.8). According to Ibn Daud, this constitutes the minimum requirements for an investigation of the Jewish religion. The “principles of religion” provide the subject matter for the second part (Eran 2019 358–660)[^eran-2019]. Here Ibn Daud is concerned with God’s existence and unity (II.1–2), divine attributes (II.3), cosmology and the heavenly intelligences (II.4), prophecy and the defense of Mosaic Law (II.5), and, finally, angelology and the problem of free will (II.6). The third and final part (Eran 2019, 661–692)[^eran-2019], deals with ethics. In this work, Ibn Daud thus offers a comprehensive survey of the contemporary philosophical debate. Due to the variety of topics covered, the book has been characterized as a compendium or a “philosophical encyclopedia in miniature” (Arfa 1954, 2)[^arfa-1954].
zh: 伊本·达乌德的书由一篇导言和长短不齐的三个部分组成。在导言中，伊本·达乌德说明：促使他写书的自由意志问题，只有在对物理学与形而上学领域的诸多问题做了预备性的哲学研究之后才能解决。在一段可称为“目录”的文字里，他在导言中列出了书中要讨论的各个专题——即初学者必须熟悉的那些专题。第一部分（Eran 2019 113–357）[^eran-2019]讨论（亚里士多德式）物理学与形而上学的基本原理。它以一个处理实体与诸范畴的逻辑章节开篇（I.1），随后依次讨论质料、形式与元素（I.2），运动与无限（I.3–5），灵魂（I.6–7），以及诸天球（I.8）。按伊本·达乌德的看法，这是研究犹太宗教的最低要求。“宗教诸原理”构成第二部分的主题（Eran 2019 358–660）[^eran-2019]。此处伊本·达乌德关心的是上帝的存在与独一（II.1–2）、神圣属性（II.3）、宇宙论与诸天界理智（II.4）、预言与摩西律法之捍卫（II.5），最后是天使论与自由意志问题（II.6）。第三部分亦即最后一部分（Eran 2019, 661–692）[^eran-2019]处理伦理学。伊本·达乌德由此对当代哲学论辩给出了一份全面综述。由于其论题之多样，此书被冠以纲要或“袖珍哲学百科全书”之名（Arfa 1954, 2）[^arfa-1954]。

en: In accordance with Ibn Daud’s concern for the harmony between revelation and reason, biblical exegesis occupies a prominent place in the *ER*. Up to the section on prophecy (II.5), the discussion of each and every philosophical topic is followed by a section in which Ibn Daud provides biblical verses that are intended to point to or demonstrate the truths of the philosophical teachings in the preceding philosophical account. In this way Ibn Daud endeavors step by step to prove that “true philosophy” does not contradict revelation. From the chapter on prophecy onwards, however, biblical passages are not provided in a separate section, but are instead interwoven into the philosophical discussion; indeed they lie at the heart of it.
zh: 与伊本·达乌德对启示与理性之和谐的关切相一致，圣经诠释在 *ER* 中占有突出地位。直到论预言一章（II.5）之前，每一个哲学论题的讨论之后都跟着一节，伊本·达乌德在其中给出圣经经文，用以指向或证明前文哲学论述中的诸真理。伊本·达乌德由此步步为营地证明“真正的哲学”并不与启示冲突。然而从预言一章起，圣经段落不再单独成节，而是织入哲学讨论之中；事实上，它们正是讨论的核心。

en: 4.2 Sources
zh: 4.2 来源

en: The “true philosophy” that Ibn Daud expounds is the form of Aristotelianism, which was articulated by the Muslim philosophers Alfarabi and especially Ibn Sina. Ibn Daud refers to Alfarabi’s commentary on Aristotle’s *Topics* and seems to have been familiar with his commentary on the *Categories* as well. In general, Ibn Daud was influenced by Alfarabi’s thought as presented in *as-Siyâsât al-madaniyya* (The Political Regime). Even more important for Ibn Daud’s system was Ibn Sina’s thought. Many of the demonstrations in the *ER* are based on works by this author, in particular his encyclopedic works *Kitâb al-Shifâ’* and *Kitâb an-Najât*. Most influential was Ibn Sina’s psychology, as well as his views of the Necessary Being, cosmology and the origin of evil. Ibn Daud also drew on the work of the critic of these philosophers, al-Ghazali (1058–1111) who summarized their teachings in *Maqâsid al-Falâsifa* (The Intentions of the Philosophers). It is most probable that Ibn Daud’s book reflects al-Najat in its purpose, organization, and language. Another source of inspiration was the Muslim theologian and polemist Ibn Hazm, whose anti-Jewish polemic inspired Ibn Daud’s Biblical exegesis. As for his Jewish predecessors, Ibn Daud built on Saadya’s *Emunot* and was certainly familiar with Judah Halevi, although he does not explicitly mention him by name (cf. section 5.7 below). Occasionally, one also comes across views that he shares with Bahya ibn Paquda, Ibn Zaddiq, or Abraham ibn Ezra.
zh: 伊本·达乌德所阐发的“真正的哲学”，是穆斯林哲学家法拉比、尤其是伊本·西那所表述的那种亚里士多德主义。伊本·达乌德提及法拉比对亚里士多德《论题篇》的注疏，而且似乎也熟悉他对《范畴篇》的注疏。大体而言，伊本·达乌德受法拉比《政治体制》（*as-Siyâsât al-madaniyya*）中所呈现思想的影响。对伊本·达乌德的体系而言，更重要的是伊本·西那的思想。*ER* 中的许多证明都以这位作者的著作为据，尤其是其百科全书式的《治疗书》（*Kitâb al-Shifâʼ*）与《拯救书》（*Kitâb an-Najât*）。影响最大的是伊本·西那的心理学，以及他关于必然存在者、宇宙论与恶之起源的看法。伊本·达乌德还从这些哲学家的批评者安萨里（1058–1111）的工作中取材——安萨里在《哲学家的意图》（*Maqâsid al-Falâsifa*）中总结了他们的学说。极有可能的是：伊本·达乌德之书在其目的、组织与语言上都反映了《拯救书》。另一个灵感来源是穆斯林神学家与论战家伊本·哈兹姆，其反犹论战启发了伊本·达乌德的圣经诠释。至于其犹太前辈，伊本·达乌德建基于萨阿迪亚的《信仰之书》，并且无疑熟悉犹大·哈列维，尽管他从未点名提及（参见下文第 5.7 节）。偶尔也能见到他与巴希亚·伊本·帕库达、伊本·扎迪克或亚伯拉罕·伊本·埃兹拉相同的看法。

en: 5. Main Themes in *ER*
zh: 5 *ER* 的主要主题

en: 5.1 Substance, Accident, and Natural Philosophy
zh: 5.1 实体、偶性与自然哲学

en: Ibn Daud’s Aristotelian orientation is immediately evident in his analysis of the notions of substance and accident, with which his book opens. Everything that is, is either substance or accident. Criticizing the neo-Platonic approach of Solomon ibn Gabirol, who held that substance and accident are relative terms, so that the selfsame thing can be a substance in one respect and an accident in another, he insists that substance and accident are absolute terms and that a thing is either a substance or an accident, but not both. The fact that certain substances derive their existence from a cause and that they can be ordered hierarchically does not detract from their substantiality: ontologically all substances are alike. This initial inquiry into the ontological constitution of existing things and the correct understanding of “substance” as that which constitutes the essence of a thing (and is thus more worthy of the term “being” than is an accident) is crucial to Ibn Daud. Besides forming the point of departure for a systematic discussion of various kinds of substances, corporeal and incorporeal, it allows him to prove that the soul is a substance, not an accident. Moreover, the distinction between corporeal and incorporeal substances introduces the reader to the existence of celestial intelligences; the incorporeal simple substances that play a central role in his thought.
zh: 伊本·达乌德的亚里士多德取向，在他对其书开篇所论实体与偶性概念的分析中即刻可见。凡存在者，非实体即偶性。所罗门·伊本·盖比鲁勒持新柏拉图主义进路，认为实体与偶性是相对的词项，因而同一事物可以在此方面是实体、在彼方面是偶性；伊本·达乌德批评这一进路，坚持实体与偶性是绝对的词项，一物或为实体或为偶性，不可兼得。某些实体从原因获得其存在、且可以按等级排序，这一事实并不减损其实体性：存在论上一切实体都是一样的。这一对存在物之存在论构造的初始探究，以及对“实体”之为构成一物本质者（因而比偶性更有资格称为“存在者”）的正确理解，对伊本·达乌德至关重要。它不仅构成对有形与无形诸类实体之系统讨论的出发点，还使他得以证明灵魂是实体而非偶性。此外，有形实体与无形实体之分向读者引入了天界理智的存在——那些在他的思想中扮演核心角色的无形单纯实体。

en: Ibn Daud’s discussion of substance and accidents includes a survey of the Aristotelian categories, which is largely based on the accounts of the Muslim philosophers. After this initial exposition, the categories are not given much further attention in the rest of the book. For our purposes, however, it is important to note that this overview of the categories is the first systematic presentation of the subject or, for that matter, of any other logical work by Aristotle, in Jewish philosophy.
zh: 伊本·达乌德关于实体与偶性的讨论包含一份亚里士多德范畴的综述，大体以穆斯林哲学家的说明为据。在这次初始论述之后，诸范畴在全书的其余部分未再受到多少关注。但就本文而言，值得注意的是：这一范畴综述是犹太哲学中对该主题——就此而言也是对亚里士多德任何其他逻辑著作——的第一次系统呈现。

en: The introduction on substance and accident leads Ibn Daud to a discussion of the question of the sense in which form and matter, the two constituents of physical beings, are substances, which allows Ibn Daud to introduce the notions of potentiality and actuality. He then proceeds to deal with other basic principles of Aristotelian philosophy, such as motion and infinity. I will not go into detail here, since Ibn Daud’s exposition does not actually provide any important new insights. Instead, his aim is to introduce the beginning student to Aristotelian physics and metaphysics. However, it is worth noting that, while earlier Jewish philosophers, such as Ibn Zaddiq, had dealt with substance and accident and other such principles, Ibn Daud is the first to do so coherently and comprehensively from an Aristotelian viewpoint. His proofs for the theses that every motion requires a mover and that the existence of an infinite series in actuality is impossible are two cases in point. The same can be said of his expositions on the soul.
zh: 实体与偶性的导论把伊本·达乌德引向如下问题的讨论：形质——物理存在物的两个构成要素——在何种意义上是实体；这又使伊本·达乌德得以引入潜能与实现的概念。他接着处理亚里士多德哲学的其他基本原理，如运动与无限。此处不拟详述，因为伊本·达乌德的阐述并未实际提供任何重要的新洞见；毋宁说，他的目标是把初学者引入亚里士多德的物理学与形而上学。然而值得一提的是：尽管先前的犹太哲学家（如伊本·扎迪克）处理过实体与偶性及此类原理，伊本·达乌德是第一位从亚里士多德视角连贯而全面地处理它们的人。他关于“每一运动都需要推动者”与“实现中的无限序列不可能存在”这两个论题的证明，就是两个适例。他对灵魂的阐述亦可作如是观。

en: 5.2 Soul
zh: 5.2 灵魂

en: The soul is an important and central issue in the *ER*, related as it is to Ibn Daud’s treatment of the aforementioned key concepts of Aristotelian natural philosophy on the one hand, and to his discussions of cosmology, prophecy and ethics on the other. About one-fifth of the book is devoted to an investigation of the soul, its nature and faculties, its relation to the body and its afterlife (*ER* Eran 2019 224–340; Samuelson 1986 88 54b–116b)[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]. Ibn Daud infers the existence of something like the soul from the fact that different natural bodies are characterized by various actions, which can only be explained by positing the existence of an immaterial principle that is added to their corporeality and from which these actions derive. Following Aristotle, Ibn Daud defines the soul as the perfection of a natural organic body that possesses life potentially. Elaborating on the distinction between soul and accident, he maintains that the soul is a substance (in the sense of form), refuting the view of the “physicians” that it is a mixture, thereby dismissing all other theories according to which the soul is an accident. In contradistinction to earlier Jewish philosophers of neo-Platonic orientation, Ibn Daud emphasizes the unity of the soul.
zh: 灵魂是 *ER* 中一个重要而核心的论题：一方面它与伊本·达乌德对上述亚里士多德自然哲学关键概念的处理相关，另一方面又与他关于宇宙论、预言与伦理学的讨论相关。全书约五分之一的篇幅用于考察灵魂——其本性与诸官能、其与身体的关系、以及其来世（*ER*，Eran 2019 224–340；Samuelson 1986 88 54b–116b）[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]。伊本·达乌德从如下事实推断出类似灵魂的某种东西的存在：不同的自然物体以不同的行动为特征，而这些行动只有通过设定一个附加于其形体性之上的非质料原理才能得到解释，诸行动皆源于此。跟随亚里士多德，伊本·达乌德把灵魂定义为潜在地拥有生命的自然有机躯体的完满。他详细展开灵魂与偶性之分，主张灵魂是实体（形式意义上的实体），驳斥“医家”把它视为混合物的观点，从而一并否定了灵魂为偶性的所有其他理论。与新柏拉图主义取向的先前犹太哲学家不同，伊本·达乌德强调灵魂的统一性。

en: A key idea in Ibn Daud’s detailed description of the various functions of the vegetative, animal and rational faculties is the notion that there is a hierarchy of soul faculties, in which the lower ones serve the higher. The speculative faculty of the human soul occupies the highest position in this hierarchy. Thanks to this faculty, which is directed towards the incorporeal world, man can perfect his knowledge and apprehend the incorporeal beings that are called angels in Scripture. It thus constitutes the link between man, angels and God. This faculty is served by the practical faculty, which is directed to the corporeal world, and governs man’s conduct. Although the soul is dependent on the body during the first stages of the acquisition of knowledge when the intellect passes from potentiality to actuality, it can exist separate from the body when it has attained the stage of acquired intellect. The rational soul is, therefore, immortal. According to Ibn Daud,
zh: 伊本·达乌德对植物、动物与理性诸官能之各种功能的细致描述中，一个关键观念是灵魂诸官能存在等级、低者服务高者。人类灵魂的思辨官能居于这一等级的顶端。凭借这一指向无形世界的官能，人可以完善其知识并把握那些在圣经中称为天使的无形存在者。它由此构成人、天使与上帝之间的纽带。服务于这一官能的是指向有形世界、支配人的行为的实践官能。虽然灵魂在求知的第一阶段——理智从潜能走向实现之时——依赖于身体，但当它达到获得性理智的阶段时，它便可以脱离身体存在。因此理性灵魂不朽。按伊本·达乌德的说法：

en: … the ultimate purpose of the creation of bodies in the physical world was that from the world of generation and corruption immaterial immortal substances would be purified. Such a substance is the human soul that is perfected by true knowledge and correct action (*ER* Eran 2019 240, #16; Samuelson 1986, 93, 65b–66b)[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986].
zh: ……物理世界中躯体被造的终极目的，在于从生灭世界净化出非质料的不朽实体。这样的实体就是人的灵魂，它由真知识与正确行动而得完满（*ER*，Eran 2019 240, #16；Samuelson 1986, 93, 65b–66b）[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]。

en: The importance of Ibn Daud’s psychology does not lie so much in its contents (that are largely based on Ibn Sina’s psychology), but primarily in its detailed treatment and in the manner in which he employs and adapts Ibn Sina’s theories so as to accommodate his own purposes. The premise that the human soul is an incorporeal substance is the key to the philosophers’ promise that internalizing intellectual and eternal truths will grant eternal life. The question of immortality is a sophisticated conversion of a theological problem into a philosophical argument regarding the eternity of truth and spiritual pleasures. It is based on Ibn Sina’s discourse on this issue, and in many cases quotes him word for word.
zh: 伊本·达乌德心理学的重要性不在于其内容（其内容大体取自伊本·西那的心理学），而首先在于其细致的处理，以及他运用并调适伊本·西那的理论以迎合自身目的的方式。“人的灵魂是非质料实体”这一前提，正是哲学家们许诺的核心——把理智的与永恒的真理内化于心，便得永生。不朽的问题，是把一个神学问题精巧地转化为一个关于真理之永恒与精神愉悦的哲学论证。它以伊本·西那对此问题的论述为据，且在许多情况下逐字引用。

en: 5.3 God and Divine Attributes
zh: 5.3 上帝与神圣属性

en: Ibn Daud deviates significantly from his predecessors since he does not deduce the existence of God from creation. In fact, as we shall later see, Ibn Daud has little to say on the issue of creation. Instead, his two proofs are based on Aristotle’s theory of motion, which presents a novelty in medieval Jewish thought. The first proof makes use of two theses that were proven in the sections on motion and infinity respectively: firstly, there is no motion without a mover, and secondly, the existence of an infinite series in actuality is impossible. On the basis of these premises, Ibn Daud establishes the existence of a first unmoved mover. Unlike Aristotle, however, he does not base the incorporeality and infinity of this first mover on the eternity of motion; an Aristotelian doctrine that he prefers to leave unmentioned. The second proof is based on the distinction between necessary and possible (or contingent) existents. The latter class of existents derives their existence from a cause. Since an infinite regress of causes is impossible, the series of contingent beings must end with the existence of an uncaused being who is called the Necessary Being and whose essence suffices for its existence. Evidently Ibn Daud considered the second to be a better proof than the first given that it yields a first principle of being, instead of merely a first principle of motion. The contrast with earlier Jewish philosophers also comes to the fore in Ibn Daud’s designations of God, such as “the first unmoved mover”, “the necessary being” or “the first cause” rather than “the Creator”. These appellations are wholly in line with his stated aim of guiding the reader to a philosophical conception of God. However, at the same time, it is evident that he identifies this first principle with the God of the Bible, an equation for which he does not provide any arguments.
zh: 伊本·达乌德与其前人有显著的不同：他不从创造推论上帝的存在。事实上，如后文所见，伊本·达乌德对创造问题着墨甚少。他的两个证明建基于亚里士多德的运动理论——这在中世纪犹太思想中是一项新事物。第一个证明利用了在论运动与论无限两节中分别证明的两个论题：其一，无推动者则无运动；其二，实现中的无限序列不可能存在。以这些前提为据，伊本·达乌德确立了第一不动推动者的存在。然而与亚里士多德不同，他并未把这一第一推动者的无形性与无限性建立在运动的永恒之上——那是一条他宁愿避而不提的亚里士多德学说。第二个证明以必然存在者与可能（或偶然）存在者之分为据。后一类存在者从原因获得其存在。既然原因的无限倒退不可能，偶然存在者的序列就必须终止于一个无因的存在者——它被称为必然存在者，其本质足以自存。显然，伊本·达乌德认为第二个证明优于第一个，因为它给出的是存在的第一原理，而不只是运动的第一原理。与先前犹太哲学家的对照，同样显现在伊本·达乌德对上帝的称谓上：“第一不动推动者”“必然存在者”“第一因”，而非“创造者”。这些称谓与他声明的目标——引导读者达致一种哲学的上帝概念——完全一致。但与此同时，显而易见的是，他把这一第一原理等同于圣经的上帝，而对这一等式未给出任何论证。

en: This God is absolutely one, both in the sense of unique (God is externally one) and in the sense of simple (God is internally one, or uncomposed). God’s unity implies that he cannot have essential or accidental attributes since that would imply plurality in the divine essence. Therefore, the attributes that are often ascribed to God, such as that he is one, existent, true, mighty etc. etc. should be interpreted either negatively, or as relations. According to Ibn Daud, “the truest predicates or attributes of God are the negations […] and although they remove many doubts, they do not convey anything” (*ER*, Eran 2019, 408, #1; Samuelson 1986, 148, 131b15–131b3)[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]. To remedy this, Ibn Daud interprets the negations as negations of something, namely of similarity, that is, as expressions of incomparability. For example, with regard to the predication of unity to God, he argues that since among all essences nothing can be found that is like God, “we know His unity in such a way that we know that His unity is not like that of any other thing that is called ‘one’” (*ER*, Eran 2019, 402, #3; Samuelson 1986, 149, 133b1–3)[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]. As for attributes understood as relations, Ibn Daud explains:
zh: 这位上帝绝对独一，既在独一无二的意义上（上帝在外部是一），也在单纯的意义上（上帝在内部是一，即无构成）。上帝的独一性蕴含：他不能拥有本质属性或偶性属性，因为那将意味着神圣本质中的多。因此，常被归于上帝的那些属性——如他是独一的、存在的、真实的、全能的等等——应当作否定式解读，或解读为关系。按伊本·达乌德的说法，“上帝最真实的谓词或属性是否定式……尽管它们消除了许多疑惑，它们却什么也没有传达”（*ER*，Eran 2019, 408, #1；Samuelson 1986, 148, 131b15–131b3）[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]。为补救这一点，伊本·达乌德把否定式解读为“对某物的否定”，即对相似性的否定，也就是不可比性的表达。例如，就“独一”这一谓词之归于上帝，他论证：既然在一切本质之中找不到任何与上帝相似者，“我们如此知道他的独一，以致我们知道他的独一不同于任何其他被称为‘一’之物的独一”（*ER*，Eran 2019, 402, #3；Samuelson 1986, 149, 133b1–3）[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]。至于被理解为关系的属性，伊本·达乌德解释道：

en: Like someone can be described, for example, in that he is the son of a certain man, and the father of a second and the uncle of a third, the maternal uncle of a fourth, the friend of a fifth and the enemy of a sixth […] this [kind of predication] is not impossible. Indeed multiple relations do not imply multiplicity in the essence of what is described by them. And in this way we can describe the Creator with many attributes since they are relations between Him and the other existents (*ER* Eran 2019 424 –426; Samuelson 1986 152 136b8–14)[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986].
zh: 正如一个人可以被描述为：某人之子、另一人之父、第三人之叔、第四人之舅、第五人之友、第六人之敌……这［种谓述］并非不可能。的确，多重关系并不蕴含被描述者本质中的多。这样我们就可以用许多属性来描述创造者，因为它们是他与其他存在者之间的关系（*ER*，Eran 2019 424–426；Samuelson 1986 152 136b8–14）[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]。

en: 5.4 Cosmogony and Intelligences
zh: 5.4 宇宙生成与诸理智

en: To explain how the plurality of the sub-lunar world can proceed from this absolutely one God, Ibn Daud presents the theory of “intermediaries”, as he found it in the works of the Muslim philosophers. This theory holds that there are secondary substances (or: heavenly intelligences) that serve as intermediaries between God and the lower world. His first step is to prove the existence of the Active Intellect, the lowest in the series of heavenly intelligences. His proof is based on the premise that the human intellect passes from potentiality into actuality, which can only be due to an agent that possesses the end of motion (that is, knowledge) in actuality. Ibn Daud then proceeds to prove the existence of other incorporeal substances, for which he likewise bases himself on the Aristotelian theory of motion, an approach that is new to Jewish philosophy. Taking the circularity of the motions of the heavenly bodies as a point of departure, he argues that the souls of the spheres in their motions pass from potentiality into actuality just as the human soul does. This motion must be caused by the intellects of the spheres that are objects of desire for their souls. The existence of heavenly incorporeal substances thus having been established, Ibn Daud goes on to describe how the lower proceeds from the higher, according to “the philosophers”. In their view, a first intelligence emanates from the One, which is similarly incorporeal, but not simple, as it has a cause, which involves composition in this entity. In a three-fold act of cognition, this intelligence produces a triad of heavenly intellect, sphere-soul and heavenly body, and this process is repeated until the sphere of the moon to which the active intellect belongs. From the various motions of the spheres, matter and forms emanate on the sub-lunar world. The details of this process are not pertinent to our current purposes. It is more relevant to note that Ibn Daud criticizes the emanation theory of the philosophers by claiming that there are no demonstrative proofs for it. In his view, they invented their theory to solve the problem of how many can come forth from one, yet, at the same time, it seems to raise more questions than it actually solves. As he puts it: “They escaped from one defamation but fell into others” (*ER*, Eran 2019, 502, #32; Samuelson 1986, 178, 159b)[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986].
zh: 为解释月下世界的多如何出自这位绝对独一的上帝，伊本·达乌德提出了“中介者”理论，那是他在穆斯林哲学家的著作中找到的。该理论主张：存在次级实体（或称天界理智），充当上帝与低级世界之间的中介。他的第一步是证明主动理智——天界理智序列中最低者——的存在。其证明基于如下前提：人类理智从潜能走向实现，这只能归因于一个在实现中拥有运动目的（即知识）的行动者。伊本·达乌德接着证明其他无形实体的存在，为此他同样以亚里士多德的运动理论为据——这一进路对犹太哲学而言是新的。以天体运动的圆周性为出发点，他论证诸天球的灵魂在其运动中如同人类灵魂一样从潜能走向实现。这一运动必定由诸天球的理智所引起——诸理智是其灵魂欲望的对象。诸天界的无形实体既已确立，伊本·达乌德接着按“哲学家们”的看法描述低者如何出自高者。按其看法，第一理智从“太一”流溢而出，它同样无形，但不单纯，因为它有原因，而原因就意味着这一实体的构成。在一个三重的认知活动中，这一理智产生一个三元组：天界理智、天球灵魂与天体；这一过程重复进行，直至主动理智所属的月球天球。从诸天球的各式运动中，质料与形式流溢到月下世界。这一过程的细节与我们当下的目的无关。更相关的是：伊本·达乌德批评哲学家们的流溢理论，声称它没有证明性的根据。在他看来，他们发明这一理论是为了解决“多如何出于一”的问题，但同时它引出的问题似乎比它解决的还多。正如他所说：“他们逃出了一种诽谤，却又陷入其他诽谤”（*ER*，Eran 2019, 502, #32；Samuelson 1986, 178, 159b）[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]。

en: Ibn Daud’s own position, however, is far from clear. There is no doubt that he accepts the notion of a hierarchical causal chain of heavenly souls and intelligences that have an influence on the heavenly world. However, he leaves his readers in the dark as to how they proceed from God, claiming that the human intellect is too limited to grasp this and that the philosophers err when they assume that the intellect can know everything. More generally, he does never address the issue of (eternal) emanation versus creation. Although he equates the God of the philosophers with the Biblical Creator, he offers no arguments in favor of creation. All that we hear is that “grand things”, such as the Ten Commandments, come directly from God. However, he fails to explain how this should be reconciled with the theory of emanation, according to which only one thing proceeds from God directly and other things indirectly. Likewise, Ibn Daud tells us in one passage that matter does not proceed from God directly; whereas in another he bluntly states that matter is God’s creation without offering any argumentation for this last statement.
zh: 然而，伊本·达乌德自己的立场远非清楚。毫无疑问，他接受天界灵魂与理智的等级因果链之观念，它们对天界世界有影响。但对于它们如何从上帝流出的机制，他让读者留在黑暗之中，声称人类理智过于有限而无法把握这一点，并且哲学家们假定理智能够知晓一切是错误的。更一般地说，他从未处理（永恒）流溢与创造的问题。虽然他把哲学家们的上帝等同于圣经的创造者，却没有为创造提供任何论证。我们听到的全部内容只是：某些“宏大的事物”，如十诫，直接来自上帝。然而他未能说明这一点如何与流溢理论相调和——按后者，只有一物直接出于上帝，其余皆间接而出。同样，伊本·达乌德在一处告诉我们质料并非直接出于上帝；而在另一处又直截了当地断言质料是上帝的创造，却未对后一断言给出任何论证。

en: Ibn Daud identifies the intelligences, which are also referred to as elevated, simple, separate or incorporeal substances, with the angels in Scripture that are intermediaries between God and man. Indeed, it is precisely their function as secondary causes that turn them into an indispensable element in his thought. Firstly, he uses the angels to avoid the unworthy notion that God should occupy himself with the particulars of the terrestrial world, which would imply plurality in divine knowledge. According to Ibn Daud, the angels are entrusted with this task. Secondly, Ibn Daud needs the notion that the angels are intermediaries for the interpretation of certain biblical texts that seem to imply a change of will in God, which is tantamount to plurality in his essence. His solution is that such verses refer not to God, but to various classes of intermediaries instead. By this interpretation, which is the outcome of philosophical reasoning, Ibn Daud also sought to counter the charges of anthropomorphism that were made by the Muslim theologian Ibn Hazm.
zh: 伊本·达乌德把诸理智——它们也被称为高升的、单纯的、分离的或无形的实体——等同于圣经中的天使：上帝与人之间的中介。的确，正是它们作为次级原因的功能，使它们成为其思想中不可或缺的要素。首先，他借助天使来避免那种不体面的观念：上帝竟要亲自操心尘世世界的诸殊例——那将意味着神圣知识中的多。按伊本·达乌德的说法，这项任务交托给了天使。其次，伊本·达乌德需要“天使是中介者”的观念，来解释某些似乎蕴含上帝意志改变的圣经文本——那无异于其本质中的多。他的解法是：这类经文指的不是上帝，而是各类中介者。借这一源自哲学推理的解释，伊本·达乌德也意在回击穆斯林神学家伊本·哈兹姆提出的拟人论指控。

en: 5.5 Prophecy
zh: 5.5 预言

en: Prophecy is another important issue in Ibn Daud’s thought, as it is the prophet who is the link between the heavenly world and man. He is the person who – thanks to his specific knowledge – must guide man towards intellectual and moral perfection. Ibn Daud’s account of prophecy immediately follows his discussion of the intelligences, since it is the Active Intellect that plays a crucial role in the explanation of prophecy. This account has a twofold aim: firstly, to provide a rational explanation of the phenomenon of prophecy and, secondly, to defend the eternal validity of Mosaic Law against Christian and Muslim claims to the contrary. Ibn Daud is, however, not entirely consistent with regard to the first objective. He begins his exposition by following the Muslim philosophers in arguing that prophecy is a natural process that is related to dreams. Basing himself on his psychology, he explains how in certain circumstances someone can receive the overflow of the Active Intellect on his imaginative faculty and intellect by which he becomes a prophet. This goal can be pursued by people with a pure soul through study and association with good people. It would thus seem that anybody who meets certain requirements will automatically become a prophet. However, in a manner reminiscent of Judah Halevi, Ibn Daud then adds that the occurrence of this phenomenon is bound to certain conditions of place, time and nation. Clearly, these stipulations are an attempt to safeguard the special character of biblical prophecy, but at the same time they impinge on the universalistic character of his psychological explanation of prophecy.
zh: 预言是伊本·达乌德思想中另一个重要论题，因为先知正是天界世界与人之间的纽带。他是那种人——凭借其特殊知识——必须引导人走向理智与道德的完满。伊本·达乌德对预言的论述紧随其关于诸理智的讨论，因为在预言的解释中扮演关键角色的正是主动理智。这一论述有双重目标：其一，对预言现象给出合乎理性的解释；其二，捍卫摩西律法的永恒有效性，以反驳基督教与穆斯林的相反主张。然而，就第一个目标而言，伊本·达乌德并不完全一贯。他的阐述开篇跟随穆斯林哲学家，论证预言是一种与梦境相关的自然过程。以他的心理学为据，他解释了在某些境况下，一个人如何能在其想象官能与理智上接受主动理智的流溢，从而成为先知。灵魂纯洁的人可以通过研习以及与善人的交往来追求这一目标。这样看来，任何满足特定要求的人都会自动成为先知。然而，以令人想起犹大·哈列维的方式，伊本·达乌德接着补充道：这一现象的出现受制于特定的地方、时间与民族条件。显然，这些限定是要维护圣经预言的特殊品格，但与此同时它们又损害了他对预言之心理学解释的普遍主义品格。

en: The defense of the eternal validity of Mosaic Law is directed against Christians, whose major claim was that the Law of Moses was replaced by the New Testament, as well as against Muslims, who believed that the Law received by Moses was falsified throughout the course of time. We do not need to review his polemics here or his use of Islamic theological arguments that prove that Moses is the only prophet who meets the requirements of classifying as a “true prophet”. What is of interest for our purpose is that Ibn Daud structures his arguments in a syllogistic framework, so as to adapt this polemical chapter to the overall philosophical outlook of the rest of the work.
zh: 对摩西律法永恒有效性的捍卫，既针对基督徒——他们的主要主张是摩西律法已被《新约》取代——也针对穆斯林——他们相信摩西所受的律法在历史进程中已被篡改。此处无须复述他的论战，也无须复述他对伊斯兰神学论证的运用——那些论证要证明摩西是唯一满足“真先知”分类要求的先知。就本文的目的而言，有意思的是：伊本·达乌德把他的论证组织在三段论框架之中，从而使这一论战性章节适配于全书其余部分的总体哲学面貌。

en: As to the place of this chapter in Ibn Daud’s book, Amira Eran has suggested that the chapter on prophecy originally formed an independent unit, which was later integrated into the *ER* (Eran 1998: 263ff.)[^eran-1998].
zh: 至于这一章在伊本·达乌德书中的位置，阿米拉·埃兰提出：论预言一章原本是一个独立单元，后来才被整合进 *ER*（Eran 1998: 263ff.）[^eran-1998]。

en: 5.6 Free Will
zh: 5.6 自由意志

en: Only towards the end of the book does Ibn Daud finally address the declared objective of his book. Thus, freedom of will seems to be an influential motto for a book that from its very first page attacks Ibn Gabirol and his eminent work, *Fons Vitae* in which *will* plays the main decisive Divine role (Eran 2023)[^eran-2023]. Ibn Daud’s theory of physical evil is to a large extent based on Ibn Sina’s approach (Eran 1989; Fontaine 2011)[^eran-1989][^fontaine-2011][^fontaine-2011-2]. It is impossible that God should be the agent of evil. The evil that is found in nature is due to matter. In fact, it is a privation, just as darkness is the privation of light. As such it is not-being and cannot be brought about by an agent. Moreover, what an individual considers to be evil can be a benefit for mankind as a whole. In line with Ibn Daud’s conception of man as a microcosm, evil in man is likewise to be ascribed to his matter and to the absence of knowledge. However, man is able to free himself from matter by means of knowledge, that is, by the actualization of his potential intellect with the help of the intelligences so as to be able to discriminate between good and evil. Another remedy for the resistance of evil lies in the Torah. Man’s choice to fight his evil inclination is neither necessary, nor impossible, but possible. To explain this, Ibn Daud states that God provided certain created things with possibility. However, the “possible” can be divided into two kinds, the first being the “possible” that is due to ignorance, for example, that the people of Spain do not know whether the king of Babylon died today or whether he is alive. To them the matter is possible because of their ignorance of what happens far away whereas in itself the matter is not possible: one of the alternatives must necessarily be true (*ER*, Eran 2019, 650, #12; Samuelson 1986, 248, 205b11–14)[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]. With respect to the second kind of the “possible,” Ibn Daud says that it is “possible”
zh: 直到全书临近末尾，伊本·达乌德才终于处理他声明在先的写作目标。于是，意志自由看起来是这部书的一个有影响的主题——这部书从第一页起就在攻击伊本·盖比鲁勒及其名作《生命之泉》（*Fons Vitae*），而在那部书里*意志*扮演着决定性的神圣角色（Eran 2023）[^eran-2023]。伊本·达乌德的物理恶的理论，在很大程度上以伊本·西那的进路为据（Eran 1989; Fontaine 2011）[^eran-1989][^fontaine-2011][^fontaine-2011-2]。上帝不可能是恶的行动者。自然中发现的恶归于质料。事实上，恶是一种匮乏，正如黑暗是光之匮乏。因此它不是存在，不能由行动者造成。此外，个体视为恶的东西，对人类整体可能是一种益处。与伊本·达乌德“人是小宇宙”的人之概念相一致，人身上的恶同样归于其质料与知识的缺乏。然而，人能够凭借知识摆脱质料——即借助诸理智实现其潜能理智——从而能够分辨善恶。对抗恶之阻力的另一个补救在于《托拉》。人对抗其恶之倾向的选择，既非必然，也非不可能，而是可能的。为解释这一点，伊本·达乌德说明：上帝赋予某些受造物以可能性。然而“可能”可以分为两种：第一种是“由于无知而可能”，例如西班牙的人们不知道巴比伦王今日已死还是尚在人间。对他们来说此事因他们对远方发生之事的无知而是可能的，但事情本身并非可能：两个选项中必有一个必然为真（*ER*，Eran 2019, 650, #12；Samuelson 1986, 248, 205b11–14）[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]。至于第二种“可能”，伊本·达乌德说它是“可能的”：

en: because God made it as “possible” and created it as something that admits of two contrary attributes, either this or that, just as it happened to be – as regards this [kind of possible] one cannot deny that God knows it as possible. And if someone would object by saying “does God not know the end of the matter?” we reply that this is not ignorance (Ibid.)
zh: 因为上帝把它造为“可能的”，把它创造成容许两种相反属性的东西——或此或彼，一如其恰好所是——就这种［可能］而言，不能否认上帝知道它是可能的。如果有人反驳说“难道上帝不知道事情的结局吗？”我们回答说：这并非无知。（同上）

en: Moreover, Ibn Daud makes use of a fourfold division of causes that he found in Halevi (*Kuzari* V.20): besides necessary causes that God knows as necessary, there are natural and incidental causes that are entrusted to secondary causes. The fourth category consists of free causes or “causes due to choice”, thanks to which man is free to choose between good and evil. In other words, God has no foreknowledge as regards human action. This rather drastic conclusion is quite unusual in Jewish philosophy; prior to Ibn Daud no Jewish philosopher was prepared to limit God’s knowledge to save the notion of free will. In Ibn Daud’s view, however, this position does not involve ignorance of God.
zh: 此外，伊本·达乌德还利用了他在哈列维（《库扎里》V.20）那里找到的四分因果：除上帝知其为必然的必然原因之外，还有托付给次级原因的自然原因与偶发原因。第四类是自由原因或“出于选择的原因”，凭借它们人可以在善恶之间自由选择。换言之，上帝对人类行动没有预知。这一相当激进的结论在犹太哲学中颇为罕见：在伊本·达乌德之前，没有哪位犹太哲学家准备通过限制上帝的知识来挽救自由意志的观念。但在伊本·达乌德看来，这一立场并不涉及上帝的无知。

en: Once man has made a choice with respect to moral conduct, the angels assist him in carrying out his choice. Moreover, the providence exercised by the angels is commensurate with man’s own efforts. In this way, the biblical verses that seem to convey that human action is determined by God are to be explained: the “hardening” of Pharaoh’s heart (Ex. 7:3) means that the intelligences helped him to persist in carrying out his own bad choices.
zh: 一旦人对道德行为做出选择，天使便协助他执行其选择。而且，天使行使的天佑与人之自身的努力相称。如此，那些看似传达“人的行动由上帝决定”的圣经经文便得到解释：法老之心的“刚硬”（《出埃及记》7:3）意味着诸理智帮助他坚持执行自己的坏选择。

en: Ibn Daud’s approach to the question of free will is not without serious difficulties. Firstly, his conception of evil as privation and as associated with matter conflicts with his initial conception of matter as a substance. Secondly, on the one hand, Ibn Daud argues that it is the intellect that chooses between good and evil, yet he also claims that the choice is a matter of man’s heart, without explaining how these two notions relate. Finally, he has nothing to say on the possibility of “repentance”, which seems to imply that man is determined as it were by his own first choice.
zh: 伊本·达乌德处理自由意志问题的进路并非没有严重困难。第一，他把恶理解为匮乏并与质料相连，这与他对质料之为实体的初始概念相冲突。其次，一方面伊本·达乌德论证是理智在善恶之间做选择，另一方面他又声称选择是人心之事，而未说明这两个概念如何关联。最后，他对“悔改”的可能性只字未提——而悔改似乎蕴含人仿佛被自己的最初选择所决定。

en: Unsatisfactory as Ibn Daud’s solution may be, he has nonetheless succeeded in removing the contradiction between biblical verses on the issue and thus in establishing harmony between philosophy and religion. It was important for him to demonstrate this harmony with respect to all the topics that led up to the question under consideration, but it is essential with respect to free will, because here philosophical speculation and religious practice intertwine. For Ibn Daud, there is no point in leading a religious life when man is not free to choose. This issue of free will therefore marks the transition from philosophical speculation to practical philosophy, which is the subject of the last part of *ER*.
zh: 无论伊本·达乌德的方案多么不能令人满意，他毕竟成功地消除了圣经经文在此问题上的矛盾，从而确立了哲学与宗教之间的和谐。对他来说，就引出所论问题的所有先行论题表明这种和谐是重要的，而就自由意志表明这种和谐则是根本的，因为在这里哲学思辨与宗教实践相互交织。对伊本·达乌德而言，当人不自由而不能选择时，过宗教生活便毫无意义。因此，自由意志问题标志着从哲学思辨向实践哲学的过渡——后者正是 *ER* 最后一部分的主题。

en: 5.7 Ethics and Religious Practice
zh: 5.7 伦理与宗教实践

en: Ibn Daud has developed a philosophic conception of God who is absolutely one and acts through intermediaries. From this God only good can proceed, whereas evil is to be attributed to matter and to man’s own bad choices. Once it has been established that man indeed has free choice with regard to moral conduct and that evil does not come from God, there is no impediment for man to opt for the good life. In his practical philosophy, Ibn Daud expounds his view of the best life. His point of departure is a description of the ethics of the philosophers, which is a combination of Platonic psychology with corresponding virtues to the concupiscent, vital and rational soul and the Aristotelian conception of virtue as the proper mean between two extremes, a model that he borrows from Muslim philosophers.
zh: 伊本·达乌德发展出一种绝对独一、经由中介而行动的哲学上帝概念。从这位上帝只能流出善，而恶则归于质料与人自己的坏选择。一旦确立了人在道德行为上确实拥有自由选择、且恶不出于上帝，人选择善的生活便再无障碍。在他的实践哲学中，伊本·达乌德阐述了他对最好生活的看法。他的出发点是对“哲学家们的伦理学”的描述——那是柏拉图式的心理学（连同与欲望灵魂、生命灵魂和理性灵魂相对应的诸德性）与亚里士多德“德性是两个极端之间的中道”之概念的组合，这一模型取自穆斯林哲学家。

en: He deviates, however, from the Platonic scheme by positing justice instead of wisdom as the supreme cardinal virtue. Man can attain bliss, the highest goal to which practical philosophy leads us, through moral perfection, which consists in perfecting his character, and in leading a good family and social life. Justice is the highest virtue for it effects harmony between the various faculties of the soul in the individual and forms the basis for man’s social life. Not only is it a philosophical virtue, but it is also a divine commandment, as can be derived from Micah 6:8. Justice indeed appears to be a key notion in Ibn Daud’s ethics, for it also provides the basis for man’s relation with God, and thus, the rationale for fulfilling the commandments of the Torah. Ibn Daud’s reasoning is as follows: once it has been established that only good proceeds from God, it is a matter of justice that man requires his benefactor by serving God. The choice to serve God is consequent upon true knowledge of God, for such knowledge automatically produces love in man, and love in turn requires action, that is, divine worship which is achieved by accepting the commandments of the Torah.
zh: 然而，他偏离了柏拉图式方案：以正义取代智慧作为最高的首要德性。人可以达到至福——实践哲学把我们引向的最高目标——途径是道德上的完满，即完善其品格，并过良好的家庭与社会生活。正义是最高的德性，因为它使个体内灵魂诸官能达致和谐，并构成人之社会生活的基础。它不仅是哲学的德性，也是神圣的诫命——这可以从《弥迦书》6:8 推出。正义看来确实是伊本·达乌德伦理学中的关键概念：它还提供人与上帝关系的基础，从而提供履行《托拉》诸诫命的理据。伊本·达乌德的推理如下：一旦确立唯有善出于上帝，那么人通过事奉上帝来回报他的恩主，就是正义之事。事奉上帝的选择源于对上帝的真知识，因为这种知识自动在人心中产生爱，而爱又要求行动，即神圣崇拜——通过接受《托拉》的诫命而达成。

en: Love and knowledge thus appear to be interrelated for one cannot love what one does not know. Intellectual love of God has fear of God, in the sense of awe, as a corollary and automatically leads man to divine worship. The Torah is the most perfect guide for leading a good moral and religious life, for it contains commandments that help man to constantly direct his actions towards God, as well as commandments that teach moral and social virtues. Moreover, it includes the so-called revelational commandments that call for obedience. Even though no rational explanation can be found for them, man must accept them once reason has established that they belong to a true revelation, which has been brought by a true and morally perfect prophet.
zh: 爱与知识由此显得相互关联：因为人不能爱其所不知。对上帝的理智之爱以敬畏上帝为必然推论，并自动把人引向神圣崇拜。《托拉》是过良好道德与宗教生活的最完美指南：它包含帮助人不断把其行动指向上帝的诫命，也包含教导道德与社会德性的诫命。此外，它还包括所谓启示性诫命——那些要求服从的诫命。即使为它们找不到合乎理性的解释，人仍必须接受它们——一旦理性确立了它们属于真正的启示、而真正的启示由一位真实且道德完善的先知带来。

en: This emphasis on religious practice in the last part of *ER* is consistent with Ibn Daud’s statement in his introduction that the goal of the study is practical philosophy (*ER*, Eran 2019 110, #16; Samuelson 1986, 42, 8b)[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]. While the bulk of the book is concerned with philosophical speculation, by the end of it practical philosophy comes to occupy center stage. This shift from philosophical speculation to religious praxis gains extra significance against the background of Judah Halevi’s attack on the philosophical worldview in *Kuzari* I.1. According to Halevi, for the philosophers the highest good is in conjunction with the Active Intellect. Once man has attained this degree, it does not matter which religion or which kind of divine worship he adopts. Although Ibn Daud does not mention Halevi by name, it is clear that he was familiar with and used his work. In fact, his work can be seen as a direct response to Halevi. Whereas Halevi regards philosophy as a threat to religion, for Ibn Daud it is indispensable for it, since the study of philosophy induces man to accept religious commandments, including those whose rationale is obscure. Therefore, despite the extensive theoretical discussions, *ER* as a whole can be seen as a work of practical philosophy. Moreover, one may argue that the book is a defense of philosophy as much as it is a defense of religion.
zh: *ER* 最后一部分对宗教实践的强调，与伊本·达乌德在导言中的陈述一致——研究的目标是实践哲学（*ER*，Eran 2019 110, #16；Samuelson 1986, 42, 8b）[^eran-2019][^samuelson-1986]。虽然全书大部关心哲学思辨，但到书末实践哲学走到了舞台中央。这一从哲学思辨到宗教实践的转变，在犹大·哈列维于《库扎里》I.1 中攻击哲学世界观的背景下获得了额外的意义。按哈列维的看法，对哲学家们来说，至善在于与主动理智的结合。人一旦达到这一程度，他采纳哪种宗教、哪种神圣崇拜便无关紧要。虽然伊本·达乌德没有点名提及哈列维，但清楚的是他熟悉并使用了其著作。事实上，他的书可以看作对哈列维的直接回应。哈列维视哲学为宗教之威胁，而伊本·达乌德视之为宗教之必需，因为哲学研究促使人接受宗教诫命——包括那些理据晦暗的诫命。因此，尽管有大量理论讨论，*ER* 整体上仍可视为一部实践哲学著作。此外，人们还可以论证：此书既是对宗教的捍卫，也同样是对哲学的捍卫。

en: 6. The Reception of *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah*
zh: 6 《崇高的信仰》的接受

en: If Ibn Daud can be regarded as the pioneer of medieval Jewish Aristotelianism, the question arises whether Maimonides, who, through his *Guide* and his prestige turned it into the dominant current in medieval Jewish rationalism, was familiar with the thought of his predecessor. Husik goes as far as to state: “We feel tempted to say that if not for Ibn Daud there would have been no Maimonides” (Husik 2002: 198)[^husik-2002]. However, Maimonides makes no explicit mention of Ibn Daud in any of his works. Yet he seems to allude to him in *Guide* I.71, when he refers to one of the earlier Jewish Andalusian thinkers whose doctrine is approximately the same as that of his own book, a description that fits Ibn Daud far better than any other of Maimonides’ Jewish predecessors. In spite of the absence of a specific mention of Ibn Daud, it is highly probable that Maimonides was familiar with Ibn Daud’s work, as the large number of similarities between the two works suggests.[^note-1]
zh: 如果可以把伊本·达乌德视为中世纪犹太亚里士多德主义的先驱，那么问题随之而来：迈蒙尼德——他通过《迷途指津》与其威望使亚里士多德主义成为中世纪犹太理性主义的主流——是否熟悉其先驱的思想。胡西克甚至断言：“我们禁不住想说：若没有伊本·达乌德，就不会有迈蒙尼德”（Husik 2002: 198）[^husik-2002]。然而，迈蒙尼德在其任何著作中都没有明确提到伊本·达乌德。不过他似乎在《迷途指津》I.71 中暗指过他——在那里他提到一位先前的犹太安达卢西亚思想家，其学说与他自己这本书的学说大致相同；这一描述与伊本·达乌德的吻合程度远超迈蒙尼德的任何其他犹太前辈。尽管没有点名提及，迈蒙尼德极可能熟悉伊本·达乌德的著作，两书之间大量的相似之处表明了这一点。[^note-1]

en: To a large extent, these points of overlap are due to their authors’ common use of theories from Islamic sources, such as the demonstrations for the existence of God. Other parallels, however, cannot be attributed to these sources, such as parallels in Biblical exegesis, in particular verses that relate to the doctrine of angels, their interpretation of the term *elohim*, and the terms *tselem* and *demut* in Gen. 1:26.[^note-2] Additional well-known Biblical interpretations that show a close affinity with Ibn Daud’s Biblical interpretations are Maimonides’ exegesis to *Exodus* 33:13–23 (appears in the first chapter of the sixth principle of the *Exalted Faith*), and the exegesis to *Jeremiah* 9:22–23 (appears in the introduction to the second part of the book (*ER*, Eran 2019, 51–54 )[^eran-2019]. Maimonides also uses similar exegeses in Chapter 54 of the first part of the *Guide* and then in Chapter 54 of the third part.
zh: 在相当程度上，这些重叠源于两位作者对来自伊斯兰文献之诸理论的共同使用，例如关于上帝存在的诸证明。然而其他平行之处无法归于这些来源，例如圣经诠释上的平行，尤其涉及天使教义的经文、他们对 *elohim* 一词的解读、以及《创世记》1:26 中 *tselem* 与 *demut* 二词的解读。[^note-2] 其他与伊本·达乌德圣经诠释显示出密切亲缘的著名圣经解读，还有迈蒙尼德对《出埃及记》33:13–23 的诠释（出现在《崇高的信仰》第六原理第一章），以及对《耶利米书》9:22–23 的诠释（出现在该书第二部分导言中）（*ER*，Eran 2019, 51–54）[^eran-2019]。迈蒙尼德还在《迷途指津》第一部分第 54 章以及第三部分第 54 章使用了类似的诠释。

en: Other shared characteristics concern the general framework and the intended audience: both works seek to guide Jews who are confused about their traditional belief as a result of the study of philosophy. Moreover, in some passages, Maimonides seems to implicitly criticize or correct Ibn Daud, for example, in his doctrine of attributes where Maimonides explicitly rejects the view that attributes that are understood as relations can be ascribed to God (cf. section 5.3 above). Maimonides says that at first sight, this kind of predication may seem permissible, but more exact speculation proves that it is incorrect, since there is no true relation between God and what is other than God (*Guide* I.52, transl. Pines 120). In general, one is tempted to assume that Ibn Daud’s work served as a model for Maimonides from which he drew inspiration on the one hand and which he found to be in need of improvement on the other.
zh: 其他共同特征关乎总体框架与目标读者：两部著作都试图引导那些因研习哲学而对传统信仰感到困惑的犹太人。此外，在某些段落，迈蒙尼德似乎在隐性地批评或纠正伊本·达乌德，例如在其属性学说中——迈蒙尼德明确拒绝“被理解为关系的属性可以归于上帝”的观点（参见上文第 5.3 节）。迈蒙尼德说，初看之下这类谓述似乎可行，但更精确的思辨证明它是不正确的，因为上帝与上帝之外者之间不存在真实的关系（《迷途指津》I.52，Pines 译本第 120 页）。总的来说，人们禁不住假定：伊本·达乌德的著作充当了迈蒙尼德的范本——他一方面从中汲取灵感，另一方面又发现它有待改进。

en: Recent research suggests that Ibn Daud’s thought has more impact on post-Maimonidian medieval Jewish philosophy than was previously assumed. M. Zonta has argued that the renewed interest in *ER* in the second half of the fourteenth century, as evidenced by the production of two Hebrew translations, had to do with the emergence of a ‘Jewish Avicennism’ during that period (Zonta 2002)[^zonta-2002]. Marginal glosses in several manuscripts of *ER* reveal that the text was actually studied, perhaps even by a group of students. The manuscript that belongs to the Montefiore Library (London 1904), 274 contains 47 folios (with 28 lines per page), of an anonymous commentary as part of the text of *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah.* According to the colophon, Elazar Parnas, who was active in Southern Italy (Reggio DiCalabria) between 1477–1497, completed to copy this supplement titled *Be’ur* in 1477. The commentary discusses philosophical issues, which appear in the first part of *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah*. It pays little attention to religious matters discussed at the end of the second part and at the third part of the book. At the end of his commentary, the author enumerates all the Biblical verses that are mentioned in the Scriptural proof texts (*Ketuvim Me’idim*) [Fontaine 2010][^fontaine-2010].
zh: 晚近研究表明，伊本·达乌德的思想对后迈蒙尼德的中世纪犹太哲学的影响大于此前所设想。M. 宗塔论证：十四世纪下半叶 *ER* 重新受到关注——两个希伯来译本的产出即是明证——与该时期“犹太阿维森纳主义”（Jewish Avicennism）的兴起有关（Zonta 2002）[^zonta-2002]。*ER* 若干抄本的旁注表明该文本确实被研读过，甚至可能是被一个学生群体研读。属于伦敦蒙特菲奥雷图书馆（London 1904）的抄本 274 含 47 张对开页（每页 28 行），是一份匿名注释，作为 *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah* 正文的一部分。按其跋记，在南意大利（雷焦卡拉布里亚）活动的以利以谢·帕尔纳斯于 1477 年完成了这份题为《注释》（*Beʼur*）的补篇的抄写。该注释讨论 *Ha-Emunah ha-Ramah* 第一部分中出现的哲学问题，对第二部分末尾与第三部分讨论的宗教问题着墨甚少。在注释末尾，作者列举了经文证明（*Ketuvim Meʼidim*）中提到的全部圣经经文（Fontaine 2010）[^fontaine-2010]。

en: Hasdai Crescas mentions Ibn Daud together with Ibn Sina and al-Ghazali as an important pre-Maimonidean author (*Or ha-Shem*, Introduction to Book I). Ibn Daud’s notion of rational love (Eran 2016)[^eran-2016] and his interpretation of Psalm 139 are likely to have influenced Crescas’ attitude to the clash between philosophy and religion (Fontaine 2024)[^fontaine-2024]. Crescas’s student Josef Albo seems to have drawn on Ibn Daud’s views (Ehrlich 2010)[^ehrlich-2010]. Y. Assudri (Assudri 2016)[^assudri-2016] has established that R. Ephraim al-Naqawah of Tlemcen (first half of the 15th century) quoted from *ER* and that R. Isaac Arama mentions him in his *‘Aqedat Yiṣḥaq* (c. 1480).
zh: 哈斯代·克雷斯卡斯把伊本·达乌德与伊本·西那、安萨里并举为迈蒙尼德之前的重要作者（《主之光》第一卷导言）。伊本·达乌德的理性之爱概念（Eran 2016）[^eran-2016]及其对《诗篇》139 的解读，很可能影响了克雷斯卡斯对哲学与宗教冲突的态度（Fontaine 2024）[^fontaine-2024]。克雷斯卡斯的学生约瑟夫·阿尔博看来也取用了伊本·达乌德的观点（Ehrlich 2010）[^ehrlich-2010]。Y. 阿苏德里（Assudri 2016）[^assudri-2016]已确证：特莱姆森的以法莲·纳卡瓦拉比（十五世纪上半叶）引用过 *ER*，而以撒·阿拉玛拉比在其《以撒之缚》（*ʼAqedat Yiṣḥaq*，约 1480 年）中提到了他。

en: 7. Conclusion
zh: 7 结语

en: Abraham ibn Daud’s importance lies in the fact that he was the first to present a coherent systematic interpretation of Judaism in light of the new challenge, namely Muslim Aristotelianism. The sustained use of Aristotelian doctrines and logical reasoning clearly distinguishes *ER* from the writings of earlier Jewish philosophers. Moreover, the manner in which he incorporates his Muslim (and to a lesser extent) Jewish sources in a carefully structured system in order to solve a religious problem is noteworthy. His thought develops along the following lines: substance – form – motion and transition from potentiality into actuality – soul – God – intelligences – prophet – freedom of the will – correspondence between correct knowledge and correct conduct – perfection.
zh: 亚伯拉罕·伊本·达乌德的重要性在于：面对新的挑战——穆斯林的亚里士多德主义——他第一个给出了对犹太教的连贯系统解释。对亚里士多德学说与逻辑推理的持续运用，清楚地把 *ER* 与先前犹太哲学家的著作区别开来。此外，他把穆斯林来源（以及在较小程度上犹太来源）整合进一个精心构造的体系以解决宗教问题的方式，同样值得注意。他的思想沿以下线索展开：实体——形式——运动与从潜能到实现的过渡——灵魂——上帝——诸理智——先知——意志自由——正确知识与正确行为之间的对应——完满。

en: Nonetheless, it should be noted that Ibn Daud’s thought contains a number of “loose ends”; the promised harmony between religion and philosophy is certainly not always achieved. Cases in point are his ambiguous position with regard to the origin and status of matter and the way in which he skirts around the issue of creation versus emanation. The inconsistencies and undetermined issues in *ER* are partly the result of the influence of neo-Platonism. The Aristotelianism of the Muslim peripatetics still contains an appreciable number of neo-Platonic notions that have made an impact on Ibn Daud. Arfa’s evaluation of Ibn Daud’s philosophic activity “at the point where it has rejected neo-Platonism but has not yet freed itself of many of its fundamental doctrines and thought habits, and on the other hand has espoused Aristotelianism but has not yet assimilated the full meaning of its world outlook” hits the nail right on the head (Arfa 1954: 4)[^arfa-1954]. For another part, the flaws in Ibn Daud’s thought are due to his conception of philosophical knowledge as the foundation on which religion should be built. For all the importance he attaches to the use of philosophical speculation, his bias is religious, which is why he prefers to remain vague about or omit Aristotelian doctrines like the eternity of motion. When harmony between religion and philosophy seems to be impossible, Ibn Daud shrinks from accepting the consequences of Aristotle’s doctrines and instead chooses to seek refuge in the limitations of the human intellect, claiming that the philosophers tend to overreach themselves. The weaknesses in his thought notwithstanding, Ibn Daud’s significance for the development of Jewish philosophy can hardly be underestimated.
zh: 尽管如此，应当指出：伊本·达乌德的思想包含若干“未结之线”；宗教与哲学之间所许诺的和谐当然并非总能达成。例证包括他对质料之起源与地位的含混立场，以及他回避创造与流溢之争的方式。*ER* 中的不一致与未定问题，部分是新柏拉图主义影响的结果。穆斯林逍遥学派的亚里士多德主义仍含有相当数量的新柏拉图主义观念，这些观念影响了伊本·达乌德。Arfa 对伊本·达乌德哲学活动的评价——“处在一个节点上：它拒绝了新柏拉图主义，却尚未摆脱其许多根本学说与思维习惯；另一方面它拥抱了亚里士多德主义，却尚未消化其世界观的完整意涵”——正中要害（Arfa 1954: 4）[^arfa-1954]。另一部分，伊本·达乌德思想的缺陷源于他把哲学知识构想为宗教应当建造于其上的基础。无论他多么看重哲学思辨的运用，他的偏向是宗教的——这就是为什么他宁愿对运动之永恒这类亚里士多德学说含糊其辞或避而不提。当宗教与哲学之间的和谐看似不可能时，伊本·达乌德畏于接受亚里士多德学说的后果，转而躲进人类理智的有限性之中，声称哲学家们往往越界。尽管其思想有这些弱点，伊本·达乌德对犹太哲学发展的重要性仍不容低估。
