A *dharma*’s capability or vertical causality, by which it facilitates the occurrence of other *dharmas* outside its consciousness series, locates it within the web of interrelations that connects it with the incessant rise and fall of other *dharmas*, and hence further individuates it as that very particular *dharma* by manifesting its unique quality and intensity of operation.
zh: 经量部与上座部结合其对说一切有部存在论模型的拒绝、以及“*dharmas* 只存在于现在”的主张，发展出了替代性的因果制约理论。经量部借“种子”（*bīja*）的观念——即后续 *dharma* 序列中的变化——解释过去与未来 *dharmas* 之间的因果互动。经量部的种子理论，是后来大乘佛教思想中两个极其重要的概念的先导，即瑜伽行派的“藏识”（*ālayavijñāna*）概念与佛性（*tathāgatagarbha*）概念（Cox 1995, 94–95；Gethin 1998, 222）。[^cox-1995][^gethin-1998]上座部的因果制约理论，如《发趣论》所述，提出了二十四缘（*paccaya*），说明一个现象在制约另一现象生起时可能运作的一切方式。二十四缘是：1）因缘（*hetupaccaya*）；2）所缘缘；3）增上缘；4）无间缘；5）等无间缘；6）俱生缘；7）相互缘；8）依止缘；9）亲依止缘；10）前生缘；11）后生缘；12）重复缘；13）业缘；14）异熟缘；15）食缘；16）根缘；17）禅那缘——特定于禅定成就的关系；18）道缘——特定于佛教道阶的关系；19）相应缘；20）不相应缘；21）有缘；22）无有缘；23）离去缘；24）不离去缘。[^note-15]上座部二十四缘中的多数在说一切有部理论中有对应者，两套体系还显示出各种其他平行的关切与相似点。那么很可能，两套体系在两部派分离之前就已起源，并在分离之后继续演进（Conze 1962, 152–153；Kalupahana 1961, 173）。[^conze-1962][^kalupahana-1961]

en: The Sautrāntika and the Theravāda developed alternative theories of causal conditioning in conjunction with their rejection of the Sarvāstivāda ontological model and their claim that *dharmas* exist only in the present. The Sautrāntika explained causal interaction among past and future *dharmas* by reference to the idea of “seeds” (*bīja*), or modifications in subsequent *dharma* series. The Sautrāntika theory of seeds is the precursor of two extremely important concepts of later Mahāyāna Buddhist thought, namely, the Yogācāra’s concepts of “store consciousness” (*ālayavijñāna*) and of Buddha-nature (*tathāgatagarbha*) (Cox 1995, 94–95; Gethin 1998, 222)[^cox-1995][^gethin-1998]. The Theravāda theory of causal conditioning, as set out in the *Paṭṭhāna*, proposes a set of twenty-four conditional relations (*paccaya*) that account for all possible ways in which a phenomenon may function in conditioning the rise of another phenomenon. The twenty-four conditional relations are: 1) root cause (*hetupaccaya*); 2) object support; 3) predominance; 4) proximity; 5) contiguity; 6) simultaneity; 7) reciprocity; 8) support; 9) decisive support; 10) pre-existence; 11) post-existence; 12) habitual cultivation; 13) karma; 14) fruition; 15) nutriment; 16) controlling faculty; 17) *jhāna* – a relation specific to meditation attainments; 18) path – a relation specific to the stages on the Buddhist path; 19) association; 20) dissociation; 21) presence; 22) absence; 23) disappearance; 24) non-disappearance.[^note-15] The majority of the Theravāda twenty-four conditions have counterparts in the Sarvāstivāda theory and both systems show various other parallel interests and points of resemblance. The likelihood, then, is that the two systems originated before the two schools separated and continued to evolve after their separation (Conze 1962, 152–153; Kalupahana 1961, 173)[^conze-1962][^kalupahana-1961].
zh: 尽管有差异，说一切有部与上座部的因果制约理论都基于这样的观念：*dharmas* 是执行特定功能的心理-物理事件，而定义什么是 *dhamma*，需要确定它做什么（Gethin 1992A, 150）。于是结果是：每一个 *dharma* 在因果条件网络中的相对定位，首先是其个体化的手段；只在次要的意义上，这一网络才是因果效力的分析。这里重现的是 *dharma* 分析作为心理事件形而上学理论的范畴维度——以条件的同一为准则。与使人能够识别和描述物质对象的时空坐标系类似，条件关系的网络可以看作在其内定位任何给定 *dharma* 的坐标系——暗示成为一个 *dharma* 就是在那个关系之网中占有一席之地的事件——这一观念令人想起唐纳德·戴维森以因果与效果的同一作为事件同一性条件的原则（2001 119–120 & 154–161）。同一种类的两个 *dharma* 例示会以完全相同的方式嵌入因果条件之网，但随后会按其独特的因果效力程度与模式被区分为个别例示。

en: Their differences notwithstanding, both the Sarvāstivāda and the Theravāda theories of causal conditioning are based on the notions that *dharmas* are psycho-physical events that perform specific functions, and that to define what a *dhamma* is requires one to determine what it does (Gethin 1992A, 150). It turns out, then, that the relative positioning of each *dharma* within a network of causes and conditions is, first and foremost, a means for its individuation. Only in a subsidiary sense is this network an analysis of causal efficacy. What reappears here is the categorial dimension of the *dharma* analysis qua a metaphysical theory of mental events in terms of sameness of conditional relations. Analogous to the space-time coordinate system that enables one to identify and describe material objects, the network of conditional relations may be seen as a coordinate system that locates within it any given *dharma*, implying that to be a *dharma* is to be an event that has a place in that web of relations—an idea reminiscent of Donald Davidson’s principle of sameness of causes and effects as a condition of identity of events (2001 119–120 & 154–161). Two *dharma* instances of the same type would fit into the web of causal conditions in exactly the same way, but would then be distinguished as individual instances on the grounds of their unique degrees and modes of causal efficacy.
zh: 6 认识论：知觉与意识过程理论

en: 6. Epistemology: Perception and the theory of the consciousness process
zh: 在试图说明什么产生解脱性智慧、什么构成觉醒之心时，阿毗达磨的探究延伸到了认识论领域。我们已经看到，阿毗达磨对有情经验的分析揭示：我们所知觉为在时间上延展的、不间断的现象之流的东西，实际上是快速发生的、因果相连的意识刹那或 *cittas*（即 *citta* 与 *caitta/cetasika* 的聚合）的序列，各有其特定对象。成熟的阿毗达磨由此把“现象在时间中由意识构成”的分析，与对意识过程的高度复杂的描述相结合，把有序意识刹那序列之间的因果关系溶解到知觉活动中。如第 2 节所述，对阿毗达磨——如同对一般佛教认识论——而言，感官知觉是知觉性、有情感的经验的范式。与每一个意识实例一样，感官知觉是有意向的，包含于感官、其相应的分别识类型与其适当的感官对象的互动之中。不过，不同的佛教部派对知觉经验的独特本性、感官与感官对象在其中的具体角色持有不同立场。上座部阿毗昙与说一切有部-毗婆沙师都持一种主张知觉意识与其感官对象直接接触的观点，后者被理解为可感性质（*sensibilia*）——因为我们知觉的不是常识对象而是其可感性质。我们可以把这一观点刻画为现象主义的实在论（Dreyfus 1997, 331 & 336）。[^dreyfus-1997]

en: In attempting to account for what effects liberating insight and what makes up the awakened mind, Abhidharma inquiries extended into the field of epistemology. We have seen that the Abhidharma’s analysis of sentient experience reveals that what we perceive as a temporally extended, uninterrupted flow of phenomena is, in fact, a rapidly occurring sequence of causally connected consciousness moments or *cittas* (i.e., assemblages of *citta* and *caitta/cetasika*), each with its particular object. The mature Abhidharma thus assimilates the analysis of phenomena-in-time-as-constituted-by-consciousness with a highly complex description of the consciousness process, dissolving the causal relations between ordered successions of consciousness moments into the activity of perception. As previously noted in section 2, for the Abhidharma, as in Buddhist epistemology in general, sensory perception is the paradigm of perceptual, sentient experience. Like every instance of consciousness, sensory perception is intentional, encapsulated in the interaction among the sense faculties, their corresponding types of discriminative consciousness, and their appropriate sense objects. Different Buddhist schools, however, held different positions on the distinctive nature of perceptual experience, and on the specific roles of the sense faculties and status of sense objects in it. The Theravāda Abhidhamma and the Sarvāstivāda-Vaibhāṣika both espouse a view that proposes a direct contact between perceptual consciousness and its sense objects, the latter being understood as *sensibilia*, for what we perceive are not objects of common sense but their sensible qualities. We may characterize this view as phenomenalist realism (Dreyfus 1997, 331 & 336)[^dreyfus-1997].
zh: 上座部阿毗昙在其注释书与手册中——主要在觉音、佛授（五世纪）与阿耨楼陀（十或十一世纪）的著作中，基于《法集论》与《发趣论》中较早的描述（*Vism* XIV 111–124, XVII 126–145；*Dhs-a* 82–106 & 267–287；*Vibh-a* 155–160；*Abhidh-s* 17–21）——阐明了其意识过程（*citta-vīthi*）理论。该理论并非独立于第 2 节所述的 *dhamma* 分类学与对 *citta* 的分析。相反，与“存在（无论范畴的还是存在论的）作为运作”的观念相一致，它把感官知觉分析为由前述分类学揭示的八十九种 *citta* 类型所执行的特定功能的结果。按这一分析，意识流中的特定功能发生在该相续的特定瞬间，因为意识的正常流动涉及心灵借助相继的几组相应心所拿起与放下感官对象。其结果是对在一系列意识刹那中于意识中生起的心理与物质现象的颇为静态的说明。[^note-16]

en: The Theravāda Abhidhamma sets out its theory of the consciousness process (*citta-vīthi*) in its commentaries and manuals, mainly in the works of Buddhaghosa, Buddhadatta (5th century CE), and Anuruddha (10th or 11th century CE), based on earlier descriptions in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* and the *Paṭṭhāna* (*Vism* XIV 111–124, XVII 126–145; *Dhs-a* 82–106 & 267–287; *Vibh-a* 155–160; *Abhidh-s* 17–21). The theory is not separate from the *dhamma* taxonomy and the analysis of *citta* as previously outlined in section 2. Rather, in congruency with the notion of existence (whether categorial or ontological) as functioning, it analyzes sensory perception as resulting from particular functions that are performed by the eighty-nine *citta* types revealed by the foregoing taxonomy. According to this analysis, the specific functions in the consciousness flow occur at particular instants of that continuum, as the normal flow of consciousness involves the mind picking up and putting down sense objects by means of successive sets of associated mental factors. The result is a fairly static account of mental and material phenomena as they arise in consciousness over a series of consciousness moments.[^note-16]
zh: 把说明限于寻常有情的意识过程，有两种过程被描述：五门过程（*pañcadvāra*）与意门过程（*manodvāra*）。它们可以相继发生，或意门过程独立发生。五门过程说明感官知觉，因为信息直接从五种身体感官的领域接收。意门过程把经由感官接收的信息内化，刻画沉浸在思想或记忆中的心。心“门”处的对象——心在佛教思想中被当作第六感官——可以是过去、现在或未来的，纯概念的甚至超越的。不过通常，意门处的对象要么是过去的记忆，要么是一个概念。如果没有知觉活动——如在深度的无梦睡眠中——心处于一种称为有分（*bhavaṅga*）的静止状态。在一生中，同一种 *citta* 执行这一不活动心的功能，它是心所回返的自然模式。当一个概念或记忆出现、而注意力未投向其他五种感官领域时，心从不活动模式切换到简单的意门过程。最简单的意门过程是下列功能的相继：1）转向思想的诸对象：持续一个刹那的功能，并被内化为所缘缘；2）速行：至多七个刹那，执行心以善或不善业主动回应对象的功能；3）彼所缘：把意识过程的对象保持一或两个刹那。

en: Restricting the account to the consciousness process of ordinary beings, two types of process are described: five-sense-door processes (*pañcadvāra*) and mind-door processes (*manodvāra*). These may occur in succession, or mind-door processes may occur independently. Five-sense-door processes account for sensory perception as information is directly received from the fields of the five physical sense faculties. Mind-door processes internalize the information received through the sense faculties and characterize the mind that is absorbed in thought or memory. Objects at the “door” of the mind, which is treated in Buddhist thought as a sixth sense faculty, may be past, present, or future, purely conceptual or even transcendent. Normally, however, the object at the mind door will be either a past memory or a concept. If there is no perceptual activity, as is the case in deep, dreamless sleep, the mind is in a state of rest called inactive mode (*bhavaṅga*). Throughout one’s life, the same type of *citta* performs this function of the inactive mind that is the natural mode to which the mind reverts. The mind switches from its inactive mode to a simple mind-door process when a concept or memory occurs and no attention is directed to the other five sense fields. The simplest mind-door process is a succession of the following functions: 1) adverting to the object of thought: a function that lasts one moment and becomes internalized as an object support; 2) impulsion: occurs for up to seven moments and performs the function of the mind’s responding actively to the object with wholesome or unwholesome karma; 3) retaining: holding on to the object of the consciousness process for one or two moments.
zh: 当一个对象出现在相应感官的“门”处时，心从不活动模式切换到五门过程中的任一种。这一感官知觉过程涉及更多功能：1）有分波动：由感官对象的刺激引起的功能。它持续两个刹那，其间发生感官接触，即感官对象对相应感官之物质的身体冲击；2）转向：持续一个刹那，其间心转向相应感官“门”处的对象；3）看：持续一个刹那，是对感官对象的纯粹知觉、只作最少的解释；4）受持：持续一个刹那，执行使通往相应分别识（视觉、听觉等）的过渡得以进行的中介角色；5）推度：持续一个刹那，执行确定感官对象之性质、并决定心对刚被识别的对象的回应的角色；6）速行：同意门过程；7）彼所缘：同意门过程。以视觉为例，视觉知觉不仅涉及看见本身，还涉及把视觉对象固定在心中、辨认其一般特征、识别其本性的一系列刹那。在意门与五门两种过程中，感官及其对象制约相应能取意识的当下刹那的生起，也就是说，这里的知觉是按同时制约来建模的。而在两种过程中，当彼所缘功能止息，心重新进入其不活动模式。

en: The mind switches from its inactive mode to any of the five-sense-door processes when an object occurs at the “door” of the appropriate sense faculty. This process of sensory perception involves a greater number of functions: 1) disturbed inactive mind: a function that arises due to the stimulus of the sense object. It lasts for two moments, during which sensory contact takes place, i.e., a physical impact of the sense object on the physical matter of the appropriate sense faculty; 2) adverting: lasts one moment, during which the mind turns towards the object at the appropriate sense “door;” 3) perceiving: lasts one moment and is the sheer perception of the sense object with minimal interpretation; 4) receiving: lasts one moment and performs the intermediary role of enabling transit to and from the appropriate discriminative consciousness, whether visual, auditory, etc.; 5) investigating: lasts one moment and performs the role of establishing the nature of the sense object and of determining the mind’s response to that object that has just been identified; 6) impulsion: same as in the mind-door process; 7) retaining: same as in the mind-door process. As an example, visual perception involves not only seeing itself, but also a succession of moments of fixing of the visual object in the mind, recognition of its general features, and identification of its nature. In both the mind-door and five-sense-door processes, the sense faculty and its sense object condition the arising of a present moment of a corresponding apprehending consciousness, that is, perception here is modeled on simultaneous conditioning. And in both the mind-door and five-sense-door processes, when the retaining function ceases, the mind reenters its inactive mode.
zh: 执行构成意门与五门过程的大部分功能的那些识类型，归入异熟 *cittas* 的范畴，即作为过去主动的善或不善意识之结果者。这意味着呈现给心灵的感官数据的经验，由一个人过去的行动决定，超出其当下的控制。每当一个人记忆或概念化、看见、听见、嗅到、尝到或触到某种可欲或愉悦的东西，他就经验到过去善意识的果报；不可欲或不悦的对象与过去不善意识则反之。只有在意识过程的最后阶段——当心已选择以某种方式主动回应其对象时——主动的当下善或不善识才运作，并构成将结未来果的业。阿毗昙由此“提供了对缘起过程的一个精确的小尺度分析”（Gethin 1998, 216）。[^gethin-1998]

en: The consciousness types that perform most of the functions that make up the mind-door and the five-sense-door processes fall into the category of resultant *cittas*, that is, those that are the result of past actively wholesome or unwholesome consciousness. This means that the experience of the sense data presented to one’s mind is determined by one’s previous actions and is beyond one’s immediate control. Whenever one remembers or conceptualizes, sees, hears, smells, tastes, or touches something that is desirable or pleasing, one experiences a result of previous wholesome consciousness. And vice versa with objects that are undesirable or unpleasing and previous unwholesome consciousness respectively. Only in the final stage of the consciousness process, when the mind has chosen to respond actively to its object in some way, actively present wholesome or unwholesome consciousness operates and constitutes karma that will bear future results. The Abhidhamma thus “provides an exact small-scale analysis of the process of dependent arising” (Gethin 1998, 216)[^gethin-1998].
zh: 说一切有部-毗婆沙师提出了类似的感官知觉说明，但主张感官对象作为实在实体存在。而经量部的知觉理论颇为不同。它立足于经量部激进的刹那论——按之没有实在的持续，只有无穷小刹那的相续——以及其因果观：原因在结果产生时即不复存在。把这些原则应用于感官知觉，就很难解释知觉如何直接取用感官对象，因为它蕴含：对象在能取识生起时已经止息。经量部的回应是：意识并不直接通达其感官对象。与现象主义的实在论相对，经量部的知觉识观可以刻画为表象论（representationalism）：它认为知觉是间接地取用其对象，经由其对象的表象性方面（*ākāra*）的中介（Dreyfus 1997, 335 & 380–381）。[^dreyfus-1997]

en: The Sarvāstivāda-Vaibhāṣika proposes a similar account of sensory perception, but argues that the sensory object exists as a real entity. The Sautrāntika theory of perception, however, is rather different. It rests on the Sautrāntika radical view of momentariness, according to which there is no real duration but only a succession of infinitesimal moments, and on its view of causation, according to which causes cease to exist when their effects come into existence. The application of these principles to sensory perception makes it difficult to explain how perception directly apprehends sense objects, for it implies that objects have ceased when their apprehending consciousness arises. The Sautrāntika reply is that consciousness does not have direct access to its sense objects. By contrast to phenomenalist realism, the Sautrāntika view of perceptual consciousness may be characterized as representationalism: it sees perception as apprehending its objects indirectly, through the mediation of aspects (*ākāra*) representative of their objects (Dreyfus 1997, 335 & 380–381)[^dreyfus-1997].
zh: 三大阿毗达磨传统——上座部、说一切有部与经量部——的共同点是：它们都表现出一种颇为相似的范式转变，即把现象的、因果受制约的世界还原为认知与意识的活动。这一转变是印度哲学更广运动的一部分：印度教、耆那教与佛教思想家转离关于外部世界与自我的本性的传统形而上学问题，转而专注于认识论、逻辑与语言的研究。其目的是对有效认知的本性与手段提供系统说明。在佛教圈子里，这一认识论转向见证了无著（Asaṅga）与世亲——瑜伽行派的创始人（400–480 CE）——以及最著名的陈那（Dignāga）与法称（Dharmakīrti）（约 500 CE）等思想家的兴起，他们发展了精密的逻辑与哲学体系（*ibid*, 15–19）。于是，阿毗达磨为这一认识论转变搭好了舞台。新的强调从毗婆沙汇编时期起成为主导，并在阿毗达磨描述 *dharmas* 本性所用术语的转变中可见。这一术语转变由“别相”（梵语 *svalakṣaṇa*，巴利语 *salakkhaṇa*）与“共相”（梵语 *sāmānyalakṣaṇa*，巴利语 *sāmānyalakkhaṇa*）两词标示。

en: What is common to all three main Abhidharma traditions—Theravāda, Sarvāstivāda, and Sautrāntika—is that they manifest a somewhat similar paradigm shift towards reducing the phenomenal, causally conditioned world into the activity of cognition and consciousness. This shift was part of a broader movement in Indian philosophy in which Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist thinkers turned away from traditional metaphysical questions about the nature of the external world and the self, and focused instead on the study of epistemology, logic, and language. Their purpose was to provide systematic accounts of the nature and means of valid cognition. Within Buddhist circles, this epistemological turn saw the rise of thinkers such as Asaṅga and Vasubandhu, the founders of the Yogācāra (400–480 CE), and, most notably, Dignāga and Dharmakīrti (around 500 CE) who developed sophisticated logical and philosophical systems (*ibid*, 15–19). The Abhidharma, then, sets the stage for this epistemological turn. The new emphasis becomes dominant from the period of the *vibhāṣā* compendia onward and is evident in a shift in the terminology used by the Abhidharma to describe the nature of *dharmas*. This terminological shift is indicated by the terms “particular inherent characteristic” (Skt., *svalakṣaṇa*, Pali, *salakkhaṇa*) and “general characteristic” (Skt., *sāmānyalakṣaṇa*, Pali, *sāmānyalakkhaṇa*).
zh: *lakṣaṇa/lakkhaṇa* 一词意为相，或把所指对象与其他对象区分开来的特定特征。逻辑学家在“定义”一个概念或逻辑范畴的意义上使用该词。阿毗达磨把它应用于观照 *dharmas* 的实践，区分一个 *dharma* 与其他 *dharmas* 共享的多个共相特征、与（至少）一个把它定义为恰恰这一个别发生的别相。藏外阿毗达磨由此把别相概念与自性概念同化。“*Dhammas*，”上座部注释文献说，“之所以称为 *dhammas*，是因为它们持其别相”（*Vibh-a* 45；*Vibh-mṭ* 35；*Paṭis-a* I 79；*Vism* XV 3），而别相“是不与其他 *dhammas* 共有的自性”（*Vism-mhṭ* II 137）。与自性并用或互换使用的别相，构成一个 *dhamma* 的唯一规定（*Vism* VI 19, 35）。它是一个 *dhamma* 作为由分立的言语描述所定义的可认知例示的认识论与语言学决定者。

en: The term *lakṣaṇa/lakkhaṇa* means a mark, or a specific characteristic that distinguishes an indicated object from others. The Logicians use this term in the sense of “definition” of a concept or logical category. The Abhidharma applies it to the practice of the discernment of *dharmas*, distinguishing between multiple generic characteristics a *dharma* shares with other *dharmas* and (at least) one particular inherent characteristic that defines a *dharma* as that very individual occurrence distinct from any other instances of its type. The post-canonical Abhidharma thus assimilates the concept of the particular inherent characteristic with that of intrinsic nature. “*Dhammas*,” the Theravādin commentarial literature states, “are so called because they bear their particular inherent characteristics” (*Vibh-a* 45; *Vibh-mṭ* 35; *Paṭis-a* I 79; *Vism* XV 3), and a particular characteristic “is the intrinsic nature that is not held in common by other *dhammas*” (*Vism-mhṭ* II 137). Used in conjunction or interchangeably with intrinsic nature, the particular inherent characteristic constitutes a *dhamma*’s unique definition (*Vism* VI 19, 35). It is an epistemological and linguistic determinant of a *dhamma* as a knowable instance that is defined by a distinct verbal description.
zh: 说一切有部-毗婆沙师的《大毗婆沙论》同样区分一个 *dharma* 的别相与共相，并把前者等同于自性，从而分辨出“在 *dharmas* 的取用或观照的诸层次”——它们澄清把 *svabhāva* 一词同时应用于个别 *dharmas* 与范畴群时遇到的歧义（Cox 2004A, 575）。以自性或以特征来描述 *dharmas* 的分析性说明之间的差别，Cox 指出（*ibid*, 576），是“自性在释经分类的语境中获得其特殊意义，而特征的出发点是透视主义的认知。两个体系都关心存在论，但从自性到特征的术语转变，反映了从基于范畴的抽象存在论到由经验或认知决定的认识论存在论的同步转变”。这一新的认识论强调，随着成熟的说一切有部释经提出的一个修正的存在定义——把一切存在之下的因果效力视为认知性的——而凸显。代表说一切有部思想史上这一发展的，是众贤（五世纪），他在《顺正理论》中说：“能生识（*buddhi*）的所缘境，是存在的真正之相。”这意味着作为我们经验世界构成成分的 *dharmas* 可以通过认知客观地识别。

en: The *Mahāvibhāṣā* of the Sarvāstivāda-Vaibhāṣika similarly distinguishes between a *dharma*’s particular inherent and generic characteristics and identifies the former with intrinsic nature, thus discriminating “levels in the apprehension or discernment of *dharmas* that serve to clarify the ambiguity encountered in the application of the term *svabhāva* to both individual *dharmas* and to categorial groups” (Cox 2004A, 575). The difference between the analytical description of *dharmas* in terms of their intrinsic nature or their characteristics, notes Cox (*ibid*, 576), is that “whereas intrinsic nature acquires its special significance in the context of exegetical categorization, the starting point for the characteristics lies in perspectivistic cognition. Ontology is a concern for both systems, but the shift in terminology from intrinsic nature to the characteristics reflects a concurrent shift from a category-based abstract ontology to an epistemological ontology that is experientially or cognitively determined.” This new epistemological emphasis looms in through a modified definition of existence proposed by the mature Sarvāstivāda exegesis that sees the causal efficacy underlying all existence as cognitive. Representing this development in the history of Sarvāstivāda thought is Saṅghabhadra (fifth century CE), who states in his *Nyāyānusāra:* “to be an object-field that produces cognition (*buddhi*) is the true characteristic of existence” (*ibid*). This means that *dharmas* as the constituents of our experiential world are objectively identifiable through cognition.
zh: 总之，正如法论及其支撑教义所示，阿毗达磨方案归根结底是认识论取向的。但该方案也意在确证：经验世界的每一个构成成分都是可知的、可名的，并且围绕对这些成分的观照而展开的话语所用的词与概念，唯一地定义其相应的所指。因此 *dharma* 分析为概念实在论铺平了道路：一种基于“真在于我们的概念与陈述，一方面，与一个独立而确定的实在的特征，另一方面，之间的符合”这一观念的世界观。概念实在论不一定蕴含这一实在作为外部存在的存在论地位。但持有这一立场，就是从最早的佛教教导——它呈现佛陀的语言观为约定性的——迈出的重要一步。[^note-17]

en: In sum, the Abhidharma project, as evident by the *dharma* theory and its supporting doctrines, is, at bottom, epistemologically oriented. Yet the project also intends to ascertain that every constituent of the experiential world is knowable and nameable, and that the words and concepts used in the discourse that develops around the discernment of these constituents uniquely define their corresponding referents. The *dharma* analysis therefore paves the way for conceptual realism: a worldview that is based on the notion of truth as consisting in a correspondence between our concepts and statements, on the one hand, and the features of an independent, determinate reality, on the other hand. Conceptual realism does not necessarily have implications for the ontological status of this reality as externally existing. But to espouse such a position is to make a significant move away from the earliest Buddhist teaching that presents the Buddha’s view of language as conventional.[^note-17]

en: the composition and transmission of early Buddhist texts is at every turn informed by stylized repetition and the use of narrative and doctrinal formulas. en: African Sage Philosophy
zh: 非洲智者哲学 sage philosophy (Dismas Masolo)

en: **First published Tue Feb 14, 2006; substantive revision Mon Feb 22, 2016**
zh: **首次发表于 2006 年 2 月 14 日；2016 年 2 月 22 日实质修订。**

en: “African Sage Philosophy” is the name now commonly given to the body of thought produced by persons considered wise in African communities, and more specifically refers to those who seek a rational foundation for ideas and concepts used to describe and view the world by critically examining the justification of those ideas and concepts. The expression acquired its currency from a project conducted by the late Kenyan philosopher Henry Odera Oruka (1944–1995), whose primary aim was to establish, with evidence, that critical reflection upon themes of fundamental importance has always been the concern of a select few in African societies. These themes involve questions regarding the nature of the supreme being, the concept of the person, the meaning of freedom, equality, death and the belief in the afterlife. The evidence that Oruka collected regarding the rational elaboration of such themes by indigenous sages is contained in dialogues, many of which appear in his classic text, *Sage Philosophy: Indigenous Thinkers and Modern Debate on African Philosophy* (1990).
zh: “非洲智者哲学”（African Sage Philosophy）是如今对非洲共同体中被视为智者的人们所产生的思想整体的通行称呼，更具体地指那些通过批判性地审查那些用来描述与看待世界的观念与概念的辩护，而为这些观念与概念寻求理性基础的人。这一表述因已故肯尼亚哲学家亨利·奥德拉·奥鲁卡（Henry Odera Oruka，1944–1995）主持的一项研究而通行，其首要目标是：以证据确立，对具有根本重要性的主题的批判性反思，历来就是非洲社会中少数人的关切。这些主题涉及关于至上存在的本性、人格概念、自由的意义、平等、死亡与来世信仰的问题。奥鲁卡收集的关于本土智者对这类主题之理性阐发的证据，保存在对话之中，其中许多对话见于他的经典文本《智者哲学：本土思想家与非洲哲学的现代论辩》（*Sage Philosophy: Indigenous Thinkers and Modern Debate on African Philosophy*，1990）。

en: 1. Oruka’s Project
zh: 1 奥鲁卡的方案

en: The following two examples from this text illustrate the method and purpose of Oruka’s questioning. When asked what he thought of his own (Luo) community’s idea of communalism, Paul Mbuya Akoko responded as follows:
zh: 该文本中的以下两个例子说明了奥鲁卡提问的方法与目的。当被问及他对自己（卢奥）共同体的公社主义（communalism）观念有何看法时，保罗·姆布亚·阿科科（Paul Mbuya Akoko）答道：

en: Now the sense in which we may justly say that the Luo in the traditional setting practiced communalism is not one in which people generously shared property or wealth. Their idea of communalism is, I think, of a co-operative nature. For example, where one person had cattle, everybody ‘ipso facto’ had cattle. For the owner of the cattle would distribute his cattle among people who did not have cattle [of their own] so that the less well-off people may take care of them…[but] never completely given away…The result is that everybody had cows to look after and so milk to drink. (Oruka, 1990: 141)
zh: 现在，我们可以正当地说卢奥人在传统环境中实行公社主义的那种意义，并不是人们慷慨地分享财产或财富的那种意义。他们的公社主义观念，我认为，是合作性质的。例如，一个人有牛，则人人“事实上”（ipso facto）都有牛。因为牛的主人会把牛分给［自己］没有牛的人，让较不富裕的人照料它们……但绝不会完全送掉……结果是人人都有牛可照看，因而有奶可喝。（Oruka, 1990: 141）

en: Another sage, Okemba Simiyu Chaungo from the Bukusu community, responded to the question, “What is truth?” as follows:
zh: 另一位来自布库苏共同体的智者奥肯巴·西米尤·查翁戈（Okemba Simiyu Chaungo）对“什么是真理？”的问题答道：

en: When something is true, it is just as you see it … it is just what it is … just like this bottle … it is true that it is just a bottle… just what it is. Truth is good. Falsehood is bad. It is evil. He who says the truth is accepted by good people. A liar may have many followers … but he is bad. [*Obwatieri* … *bwatoto*. *Bwatoto nokhulola sindu ne siene sa tu … nga inchpa yino olola ichupa ni yene sa tu*.] (*Sage Philosophy*, p. 111)
zh: 当某物为真时，它就是你看到的样子……它就是它所是的样子……就像这个瓶子……说它只是一个瓶子是真的……它就是它所是的样子。真理是好的。虚假是坏的。它是恶。说真话的人被好人接受。说谎者可能有很多追随者……但他是坏的。［*Obwatieri* … *bwatoto*. *Bwatoto nokhulola sindu ne siene sa tu … nga inchpa yino olola ichupa ni yene sa tu*.］（*Sage Philosophy*, p. 111）

en: And in response to an Interlocutor, who asks “Why would people tell lies?”, he responded:
zh: 而当对话者问“人们为什么撒谎？”时，他答道：

en: So that they may eat… so that they may get empty prestige. They want to profit fraudulently. (*Sage Philosophy*, p. 111)
zh: 为了吃……为了得到空洞的虚荣。他们想欺诈获利。（*Sage Philosophy*, p. 111）

en: From these examples some of the distinguishing characteristics of Sage Philosophy can be gleaned. First, they display the deeply personal nature of the ideas, or opinions, that the sages expressed in response to the questions. Akoko’s insight derives from his individual reflections on the practice of communalism to consider its justification. Second, they provide evidence of abstract thought about philosophic topics. Chaungo considers what it means for a proposition to be true and expresses what turns out to be a correspondence theory of truth — according to which the proposition “This is a bottle” is true if the object it refers to, this thing, is indeed a bottle. By pointing out that some people choose deliberately to be untruthful for unjust gain he also addresses the moral aspects of truth.
zh: 从这些例子可以窥见智者哲学的一些区辨性特征。第一，它们显示了智者们在回答问题时所表达的思想或意见的深刻的个人性。阿科科的洞见源于他对公社主义实践之辩护的个人反思。第二，它们提供了对哲学主题之抽象思想的证据。查翁戈考虑了一个命题为真意味着什么，并表达了结果上是一种真理符合论的东西——按之，命题“这是一个瓶子”为真，当它所指称的对象、这个东西，确实是一个瓶子。通过指出有些人为了不义之利而故意选择不诚实，他也论及了真理的道德方面。

en: Oruka’s survey of sages aimed to counter three negative claims regarding the philosophical status of indigenous African thought:
zh: 奥鲁卡对智者们的调查，意在反驳关于本土非洲思想之哲学地位的三项否定性主张：

en: Unlike Greek sages who used reason, African sages do not engage in philosophic thought. African sages are part of an oral tradition, whereas philosophic thought requires literacy. African traditions encourage unanimity regarding beliefs and values and discourage individual critical thought.
zh: 与运用理性的希腊智者不同，非洲智者不从事哲学思考。 非洲智者属于口传传统，而哲学思想需要文字。 非洲传统鼓励在信念与价值上的一致，抑制个人的批判性思想。

en: His reply to these claims has significantly shaped the discourse on Sage Philosophy. In what follows the criteria he proposed to determine what counts as Sage Philosophy will be considered in the light of his critique of the Eurocentric bias against African philosophic thought and the question of whether literacy is required.
zh: 他对这些主张的回应，显著地塑造了关于智者哲学的话语。下文将结合他对反非洲哲学思想的欧洲中心偏见的批判、以及文字是否必需的问题，来考察他提出的判定何为智者哲学的判准。

en: 2. The African Sage Tradition and Eurocentric Bias
zh: 2 非洲智者传统与欧洲中心偏见

en: First, Oruka was concerned about the picture created under colonialism that, while the sayings of numerous Greek sages such as Thales, Anaximander, Heraclitus, and other pre-Socratics, were regarded as “philosophical,” those of traditional African sages were not. This bias arises out of the implicit belief that philosophy is the privileged activity of certain races. He believed that this unjustified belief had further led to the image of philosophy as the restricted property of Greeks, or Europeans, and, even more exclusively, the property of white males. Partly concerned with exposing the falsehood of this Eurocentric attitude, he recognized that what had raised the apparently simple sayings of the pre-Socratics to the status of philosophy was the subsequent sustained commentaries by later philosophers. He maintained that the ideas expressed by indigenous African sages were no different from those by the earlier Greeks. When recorded later in books, the sayings of Greek sages came to be widely regarded as “philosophical,” and the people who produced them as “philosophers.” Given such a scenario, Oruka was led to wonder, why would the sayings of Akoko, or those of Chaungo, for example, not be similarly regarded after they are committed to writing by a professional philosopher?
zh: 首先，奥鲁卡关注的是殖民主义之下造成的一幅图景：色诺芬尼、赫拉克利特与其他前苏格拉底哲人等众多希腊智者的言论被视为“哲学的”，而传统非洲智者的言论却不被如此看待。这种偏见出于一个隐含的信念：哲学是某些种族的特权活动。他相信，这一无据的信念进一步造成了哲学是希腊人或欧洲人的专属财产、甚至更排他地是白人男性之财产的形象。部分出于揭露这种欧洲中心态度之虚妄的考虑，他认识到：把前苏格拉底哲人那些表面上简单的言论抬举到哲学地位的，是后来哲学家们持续不断的注释。他坚持认为，本土非洲智者所表达的思想与早期希腊人所表达的思想并无不同。当希腊智者的言论后来被记入书册时，它们开始被广泛视为“哲学的”，其创造者则被视为“哲学家”。在这样的情形下，奥鲁卡不禁追问：阿科科的言论，或查翁戈的言论，在由职业哲学家笔录成书之后，为什么不应当得到类似的对待？

en: Oruka supports his comparison of indigenous African sages with the pre-Socratics by citing two methods that have contributed to the growth of philosophy in the West, beginning with its Greek roots. One direct method of using dialogues is exemplified in the early Platonic works. Socrates asks primary questions upon which the exposition of ideas by his interlocutor is based. Oruka viewed his own dialogues with the sages as an example of this practice in the African context. Socrates regarded himself as a “mid-wife” of sorts, because he merely helped those with the knowledge to bring it out. He brought out what was in each case really the property of his interlocutors, not his own. Oruka meant his dialogues, in similar fashion, to capture both this method and its outcome. He maintained that the sages he and his disciples interviewed were the owners of their own ideas. The Western-trained philosopher, he says, “plays the role of philosophical provocation” (*Sage Philosophy*, p. 47). The other method, exemplified in the later Platonic works, involves indirect engagement with the sayings of the sages through a commentary on their ideas — derived from these dialogues, or from general acquaintance with the sages’ views. Oruka believed that, by these two methods, the growth of African philosophy can take place in a manner similar to the growth of Western philosophy. Underlying Oruka’s position was his hope that trained philosophers, regardless of their origins, could take on the sages on their claims in their commentaries and critiques as this is how advancement and growth of knowledge partly takes place. This is to say, in hindsight, that even in Oruka’s own view the sayings of the sages were not free of critique.
zh: 奥鲁卡通过引用两种方法，来支持他把本土非洲智者与前苏格拉底哲人的比较——这两种方法自希腊源头起促进了西方哲学的成长。使用对话的直接方法，例证于柏拉图的早期著作。苏格拉底提出基本问题，对话者的观念阐发即以此为基础。奥鲁卡把他自己与智者们的对话视为这一实践在非洲语境中的实例。苏格拉底自视为某种“助产士”，因为他只是帮助有知识的人把知识引出来。他引出的在每一种情形中其实都是对话者的所有物，而不是他自己的。奥鲁卡的对话同样意在捕捉这一方法及其成果。他主张，他与弟子们访谈的智者是其自身思想的所有者。他说，受过西方训练的哲学家“扮演哲学激发者的角色”（*Sage Philosophy*, p. 47）。另一种方法例证于柏拉图的后期著作：通过对其思想的注释——得自这些对话、或对智者们观点的一般了解——间接地介入智者们的言论。奥鲁卡相信，借助这两种方法，非洲哲学可以像西方哲学的成长那样成长。支撑奥鲁卡立场的，是他的希望：受过训练的哲学家，无论出身，都可以在其注释与批评中就智者们的主张与之交锋，因为知识的推进与成长部分正是这样发生的。这就是说，事后看来，即便在奥鲁卡自己的观点里，智者们的言论也不是免于批评的。

en: 3. Literacy and The Oral Tradition in Sage Philosophy
zh: 3 智者哲学中的文字与口传传统

en: The influence of colonial bias against unwritten thought was also challenged by Oruka’s project. By publishing his interviews with the sages he aimed to counter the second negative claim regarding the denigration of African thought, namely that “philosophy is and can only be a ‘written’ enterprise; and so a tradition without writing is incapabale of philosophy [and that any claim to the contrary] …is a non-scientific, mythological claim” (*Sage Philosophy*, p.xv). He insisted that there are African thinkers, not yet absorbed into the tradition of the written word, whose memories are, in terms of consistency and organization, as good as the information recorded in books (*Sage Philosophy*, pp. 49–50). Responding to adversaries, he cautioned that:
zh: 奥鲁卡的方案也挑战了殖民偏见对无文字思想的贬抑。通过发表他对智者们的访谈，他意在反驳关于贬抑非洲思想的第二项否定主张，即“哲学是且只能是一种‘书写的’事业；因此一个没有文字的传统是没有哲学能力的［而任何相反的主张］……是一条非科学的、神话式的主张”（*Sage Philosophy*, p.xv）。他坚持：有一些尚未被文字传统吸纳的非洲思想家，其记忆在一致性与条理性方面，不亚于记在书中的信息（*Sage Philosophy*, pp. 49–50）。回应论敌时，他告诫说：

en: to argue like the critics, not just of Sage philosophy but of African philosophy generally have done that Africa is having a late start in philosophy just because we have no written records of her past philosophical activities is, wrongfully, to limit the sources from which we could detect traces of such activities. (*Sage Philosophy*, p. 50)
zh: 像智者哲学乃至整个非洲哲学的批评者们那样论证——说非洲在哲学上起步晚，只因为我们没有关于其过往哲学活动的书面记录——是不正当地限制了我们可以从中发现这类活动之踪迹的来源。（*Sage Philosophy*, p. 50）

en: Peter Bodunrin was particularly critical of Oruka’s method of extracting Sage Philosophy. He argued that to show that there were people, like the indigenous sages, who were capable of philosophical thinking was one thing, but it was a completely different thing to show that there were African philosophers who have engaged in organized systematic reflections on the traditions of their people. Regarding Bodunrin’s first objection, Oruka’s response, as already indicated above, was that philosophers often work in response to other ideas, whether they are the ideas of other philosophers, or popular ideas in the philosopher’s own setting. Oruka had a relatively longer response to Bodunrin’s second objection. In another essay popularly associated with his name, Oruka identified four main trends to be constitutive of African philosophy, namely (i) African ethnophilosophy, (ii) African nationalist-ideological philosophy, (iii) professional African philosophy, and of course, (iv) the African Sage philosophy under consideration here. Not only do these trends show different approaches that African philosophers have adopted to unravel and systematically to expose the underlying principles on which different departments of African life are based, they also demonstrate that African philosophy is not limited or confined to the academic institutions.
zh: 彼得·博敦林（Peter Bodunrin）对奥鲁卡提取智者哲学的方法批评尤力。他论证说，表明存在像本土智者那样能够进行哲学思考的人是一回事，而表明存在曾对人民的传统进行过有组织的系统反思的非洲哲学家，是完全不同的另一回事。关于博敦林的第一项反驳，奥鲁卡的回应——如上所述——是：哲学家常常是在回应其他观念中工作的，无论那些观念是别的哲学家的观念，还是哲学家所处环境中的流行观念。对博敦林的第二项反驳，奥鲁卡有相对更长的回应。在另一篇常与其名相联的文章中，奥鲁卡认定四个主要趋势构成非洲哲学，即（i）非洲民族哲学，（ii）非洲民族主义-意识形态哲学，（iii）职业非洲哲学，当然还有（iv）此处讨论的非洲智者哲学。这些趋势不仅显示了非洲哲学家为揭示并系统地呈现非洲生活各部门所依据的底层原则而采取的不同进路，也表明非洲哲学并不限于学院机构之内。

en: Indeed, many African philosophers look far beyond the traditional philosophical texts for sources and subject matter of philosophical reflection. For example, while engaging in subtle analytic philosophical reflections, African philosophers incorporate with great ease narratives from everyday lives and from literature into their reflections of the philosophical implications of their cultural events. Oruka was especially wary of the sub-group among professional African philosophers whose position regarding African traditional modes of thought was analogous to European bias in denying reason to Africans in their traditional settings. It was this attitude, according to Oruka, that amounted to a claim that Africans lacked a tradition of organized systematic philosophical reflections on the thoughts, beliefs, and practices of their own people. He thought that this view was exemplified in its most eloquent and strongest form by Peter Bodunrin. In his (Oruka’s) own estimation, Bodunrin had seriously underestimated the central point in the long tradition of Western scholarship, popularized by the works of Lévy-Bruhl, that denied Africans not only the existence of organized systematic philosophical reflection, but reason itself. Oruka thought that this view was rather absurd, for no society of humans can live for any reasonable amount of time, let alone making any advances in their own ways of seeing and doing things, if they do not have reason, or if the ideas and concepts upon which their cultures are built do not make sense. If, on the other hand, critics of African Sage philosophy based their refutation of the possibility of sage philosophy on the lack of written philosophical treatises, Oruka countered such a position by arguing that to exist as a philosopher it is not necessary that one’s thoughts must be written, or that they must progress — meaning that they must be commented on or even be available to future generations. While systematicity is important to the structure and consistency of good thinking, neither it nor preservation of thought necessarily requires literacy. Preservation in particular, he thought, was done selectively by generations for divers emerging reasons and circumstances, and so was not, in and of itself, the measure of the philosophical quality of someone’s thoughts. For just as thoughts can be expressed either in writing, or as unwritten oral reflections, e.g., sayings and argumentations of sages, so they may be preserved for a long time by sages, or quickly forgotten and cast into historically insignificant bits of a community’s past, only to be remembered by the few whom they touched in some special way.
zh: 事实上，许多非洲哲学家为哲学反思的来源与主题，远超传统的哲学文本去寻找。例如，在进行细密的分析哲学反思的同时，非洲哲学家们极其自然地把来自日常生活与文学的叙事纳入他们对文化事件的哲学意蕴的反思之中。奥鲁卡尤其警惕职业非洲哲学家中的这样一个亚群体：他们对非洲传统思想模式的立场，相当于否认非洲人在其传统环境中拥有理性的欧洲式偏见。按奥鲁卡的看法，正是这种态度等于主张：非洲人缺乏对其民族自身的思想、信念与实践进行有组织的系统哲学反思的传统。他认为这一观点最雄辩、最强有力的例证就是彼得·博敦林。按他（奥鲁卡）自己的估计，博敦林严重低估了由列维-布留尔的著作发扬光大的西方学术悠久传统的核心要点——这一传统不仅否认非洲人存在有组织的系统哲学反思，而且否认理性本身。奥鲁卡认为这一观点相当荒谬：任何一个人类社会，如果缺乏理性，或者如果其文化赖以建立的观念与概念毫无意义，就不可能延续任何合理的时间，遑论在其看待与行事的方式上取得任何进展。另一方面，如果非洲智者哲学的批评者把对智者哲学可能性的驳斥建立在书面哲学论著的缺乏之上，奥鲁卡则回应说：要作为一个哲学家存在，其思想不必被写下来，也不必有所推进——意思是它们不必被评论，甚至不必为后代所及。虽然系统性对良好思考的结构与一致性很重要，但它与思想的保存都不必然需要文字。保存尤其如此，他认为那是世代出于多样的理由与境况而有选择地进行的，因此它本身并不是某人之思想之哲学品质的尺度。因为正如思想既可写下来表达，也可作为未书写的口传反思——例如智者的箴言与论证——来表达，它们也可能被智者长期保存，或被迅速遗忘、抛入共同体过去的历史上无关紧要的碎屑之中，只被少数以某种特殊方式被它们触动的人记得。

en: Oruka’s position, as is also argued forcefully by Kwasi Wiredu, another African philosopher and Oruka’s contemporary, is that there is no harm in African philosophers’ creative fusion of influences from other traditions into their critical evaluations of African beliefs and practices in different fields (“The Ghanaian Tradition of Philosophy” in *Person and Community*, p. 2). Such a fusion is part of bringing into focus the interplay between philosophy and practice. Oruka believed, as he explains in *Trends in Contemporary African Philosophy* (pp. 17–18), that this is precisely what Kwame Nkrumah (1964), Léopold S. Senghor (1962), and Julius K. Nyerere (1968, 1968a), for example, had done in forming their political-philosophical positions (what Oruka calls “ideological trends”), all with different results.
zh: 奥鲁卡的立场——另一位非洲哲学家、奥鲁卡的同代人夸西·维雷杜（Kwasi Wiredu）也力主之——是：非洲哲学家把来自其他传统的影响创造性地融合进他们对不同领域中非洲信念与实践的批判性评价，并无损害（“The Ghanaian Tradition of Philosophy” in *Person and Community*, p. 2）。这种融合正是把哲学与实践的交互带入焦点的一部分。奥鲁卡相信，正如他在《当代非洲哲学诸趋势》（pp. 17–18）中所解释的，这正是克瓦米·恩克鲁玛（Kwame Nkrumah，1964）、利奥波德·S. 桑戈尔（Léopold S. Senghor，1962）与朱利叶斯·K. 尼雷尔（Julius K. Nyerere，1968, 1968a）等人形成其政治-哲学立场（奥鲁卡称之为“意识形态趋势”）时所做的，尽管结果各异。

en: 4. Ethnophilosophy, Unanimity and African Critical Thought
zh: 4 民族哲学、一致性与非洲批判性思想

en: Although it had been used previously by other writers, the term “ethnophilosophy” acquired its notoriety in the work of the Beninois philosopher Paulin Hountondji (1970, 1983). Perhaps unaware that the term had been used earlier, Hountondji criticized the Belgian missionary, Placide Tempels’ book, *Bantu Philosophy* (first French ed. 1945, and Eng. tr. 1959), as well as his disciples, among them the French philosopher and ethnographer Marcel Griaule, the Rwandais philosopher Alexis Kagame, and the Kenyan theologian John Mbiti, for casting African philosophy as an anonymous system of thought, without individual thinkers to claim or account for it. By the end of the 1960s, the positive reception in Anglophone Africa, not only of Tempels’ Bantu Philosophy, but also John Mbiti’s *African Religions and Philosophy* (1969) and Marcel Griaule’s *Conversations with Ogotemmêli* that had recently been translated into English (1965), coincided with the rising tides of political and cultural nationalism throughout the continent.
zh: 虽然此前已被其他作者使用，“民族哲学”（ethnophilosophy）一词的恶名是在贝宁哲学家保利恩·洪通吉（Paulin Hountondji，1970, 1983）的著作中获得的。或许不知道这个词此前已被使用，洪通吉批评比利时传教士普拉德·滕佩尔斯（Placide Tempels）的著作《班图哲学》（法文初版 1945，英译 1959），以及他的追随者——其中有法国哲学家与民族志学家马塞尔·格里奥勒（Marcel Griaule）、卢旺达哲学家阿莱克西·卡加梅（Alexis Kagame）与肯尼亚神学家约翰·姆比蒂（John Mbiti）——把非洲哲学呈现为一个匿名的思想体系，没有个人的思想家来认领或说明它。到 1960 年代末，英语非洲对滕佩尔斯《班图哲学》、以及对约翰·姆比蒂《非洲宗教与哲学》（1969）与马塞尔·格里奥勒刚被译成英文（1965）的《与奥戈特默利对话》的积极接受，与整个大陆高涨的政治与文化民族主义浪潮同步。

en: The third negative claim Oruka aimed to challenge pertains to the philosophical status of indigenous African thought. Ethnophilosophy had falsely popularized the view that traditional Africa was a place of philosophical unanimity and that African traditions encouraged unanimity regarding beliefs and values. If this were true it would allow no room for individual thinkers like, say, Socrates or Descartes, with their own independent views on such matters. Oruka was concerned that African intellectuals were drawn into this false assumption regarding the intellectual inclination of African people, maintaining the belief that critique is absent from indigenous African thought. This situation was worsened by the new political movements of postindependence African nations where one-party political systems sprang up. By outlawing opposition politics as being both unAfrican and antinationalist, political leaders often appealed to this view of unanimity. The Sage Philosophy project objected to this claim regarding unanimity in Africa, which Oruka regarded as absurd, by presenting empirical evidence of the diversity of thought among indigenous thinkers. Oruka insisted that, while rulers everywhere will always crave unanimity, thinkers thrive in dialogue and diversity of opinion. He pointed out that Sage philosophy was about thinkers, not rulers.
zh: 奥鲁卡意在挑战的第三项否定主张，关乎本土非洲思想的哲学地位。民族哲学错误地普及了这样一种观点：传统非洲是一个哲学上全体一致的地方，非洲传统鼓励在信念与价值上的一致。如果这是真的，它就不会给像苏格拉底或笛卡尔那样持有独立观点的个别思想家留下余地。奥鲁卡担心非洲知识分子被拉进这一关于非洲人民思想倾向的错误假定之中，维持着“本土非洲思想中缺乏批评”的信念。独立后非洲国家一党制政治体制的兴起使这一情形更加恶化。政治领袖们把反对派政治定为既非非洲又反民族的东西而加以取缔时，常常诉诸这种一致观。智者哲学方案通过呈现本土思想家思想多样性的经验证据，反对这一关于非洲一致性的主张——奥鲁卡视之为荒谬。他坚持：统治者无论何处都永远渴望一致，而思想者在对话与意见多样性中繁荣。他指出，智者哲学关乎的是思想者，不是统治者。

en: Oruka’s desire to distinguish Sage philosophy from ethnophilosophy was also in response to another false view, partly created by ethnophilosophy, that indigenous African thought is anonymous. An important charge against ethnophilosophy has been that, by simply presenting the teachings of African beliefs in the allegorical modes, the impression is created that indigenous African modes of thought are deeply grounded in their mythical representations of reality, thus leaving the philosophic ideas largely unexplained. With this in mind, Oruka’s project aimed to counter two types of false perception of indigenous African thought. First, he separated the myths from the clearly thought out and logically valid philosophical ideas of indigenous individual thinkers to make clear what he frequently referred to as the “anthropological fogs” (*Sage Philosophy*, pp. xxi-xxix). Secondly, he contested the idea that a qualitative mental leap from myth is required for Africans to embrace philosophical thought. Such a view had been expressed by the Belgian philosopher Franz Crahay in a widely read article, “Le décollage conceptuel: conditions d’une philosophie bantoue” (1965). Although he was critical of ethnophilosophy, Hountondji was the first philosopher to distance himself from Crahay’s position, arguing that local knowledge systems were already separate from myths, as no humans can live on myths. Moral principles, for example, would have to be abstract in character to be applicable in general terms beyond one person (Hountondji 1970)[^hountondji-1970]. According to Wiredu (1996: 182ff), such independent and critical thinking was available in varying forms in Akan communities and was the basis of frequently protracted disputations among elders in search of a consensus regarding matters that required negotiations. Thus, contrary to the view that knowledge at the communal level was anonymous, Wiredu argues that it is precisely in regard to the importance of consensus on matters of common good that disputation and careful navigation through different opinions was not just considered to be crucial, but was put on transparent display until some form of consensus was attained. In other words, consensus was not imposed, but relentlessly pursued. Such important matters like just claims to different kinds of rights were not adjudicated without the input of those members of community who were well regarded for their independent opinions.
zh: 奥鲁卡想把智者哲学与民族哲学区分开的愿望，也是对另一错误看法——部分由民族哲学造成，即本土非洲思想是匿名的——的回应。针对民族哲学的一项重要指控一直是：仅仅以寓意的模式呈现非洲信念的教导，就造成了一种印象，即本土非洲的思想模式深深植根于其对实在的神话表象之中，从而让哲学观念大体未经解释。有见于此，奥鲁卡的方案旨在反驳对本土非洲思想的两种错误感知。第一，他把神话与本土个别思想者的清晰思考过的、逻辑上有效的哲学观念区分开来，以澄清他常说的“人类学的雾”（*Sage Philosophy*, pp. xxi-xxix）。其次，他质疑这样一种观念：非洲人要接受哲学思想，需要一次从神话出发的质的飞跃。这种观点曾由比利时哲学家弗朗茨·克拉艾（Franz Crahay）在一篇流传甚广的文章“Le décollage conceptuel: conditions d'une philosophie bantoue”（1965）中表达。虽然他对民族哲学持批评态度，洪通吉却是第一位与克拉艾立场拉开距离的哲学家，他论证：地方知识体系早已与神话分离，因为没有人能靠神话生活。例如，道德原则必须具有抽象的性质，才能超出一个人而以一般的方式适用（Hountondji 1970）。[^hountondji-1970]按维雷杜（1996: 182ff）的说法，这种独立的批判性思考在阿肯共同体中以不同形式可得，并且是长老之间就需要协商的事务寻求共识时常见的旷日持久的争辩的基础。因此，与“共同体层面的知识是匿名的”这一观点相反，维雷杜论证：恰恰是在就共同善之事达成共识的重要性上，争辩与在不同意见间的仔细周旋不仅被视为关键，而且被透明地展示出来，直到达成某种形式的共识。换言之，共识不是强加的，而是不懈追求的。诸如对不同种类的权利的正当主张这类重要事务，未经那些以其独立意见而受敬重的共同体成员的参与，不会被裁断。

en: Another point that Oruka makes against the perception of unanimity in African traditional thought can be found in the expressions of thinkers whose ideas are grounded in critical analysis and evaluation of everyday experiences in their communities. Another example of this, besides such figures as Paulo Mbuya Akoko and others who Oruka mentions and discusses in the book *Sage Philosophy* is the famous Swahili poet, critic, and philosopher Shabaan bin Robert from then Tanganyika, now Tanzania. Shabaan, famed as a pioneer in the interface between the oral and the written traditions, has established a unique legacy as an indigenous independent thinker, whose focus in his written work was to theorize about metaphysical and social ideals. About the former, Shabaan theorizes in his work entitled *Utubora Mkulima* the attributes of ideal personhood by arguing strongly, in a dialogical setting, that an ideal person is one whose moral righteousness is aimed at being a perfect member of community, and therefore his concerns for common good supersede individual interests (pp. 26–28). Regarding social ideals, Shabaan argues in *Kusadikika* that a good society is defined as one in which all members are accorded their basic rights and treated with equality regardless of gender, age, or social status (pp. 29–43). This makes Shabaan Robert an example of a liberal thinker whose ideas bridge between indigenous or pre-colonial social structures and values, and the so-called modern society whose values were significantly influenced by colonial occupations and interests, as well as new economic, political, and moral values. In these senses, Shabaan Robert thought and works complement those of other indigenous thinkers in critiquing both indigenous and new modes of existence. To Oruka, these are signs that indigeneity is not, as is widely but falsely thought, synonymous with anonymity and stagnation in thought.
zh: 奥鲁卡针对非洲传统思想之一致观提出的另一点，可见于其思想植根于对其共同体日常经验的批判分析与评价的思想家们的表达。除了奥鲁卡在《智者哲学》一书中提及并讨论的保罗·姆布亚·阿科科等人物之外，另一个例子是当时属坦噶尼喀、今属坦桑尼亚的著名斯瓦希里诗人、批评家与哲学家沙班·宾·罗伯特（Shabaan bin Robert）。沙班以口传与书面传统之交界的先驱著称，作为本土的独立思想家留下了独特的遗产，其文字工作的重心是对形而上学与社会理想作理论化。关于前者，沙班在其题为《乌图博拉·姆库利马》（*Utubora Mkulima*）的著作中，在对话性的场景里有力地论证了理想人格的诸属性：一个理想的人是其道德正义以成为共同体的完美成员为目标的人，因此其对共同善的关切超越个人利益（pp. 26–28）。关于社会理想，沙班在《库萨迪基卡》（*Kusadikika*）中论证：一个好的社会定义为其中所有成员都被赋予基本权利、不因性别、年龄或社会地位而被区别对待的社会（pp. 29–43）。这使得沙班·罗伯特成为一个自由主义思想家的例子，其思想桥接本土的或前殖民的社会结构与价值，以及其价值深受殖民占领与利益、以及新的经济、政治与道德价值影响的所谓现代社会。在这些意义上，沙班·罗伯特的思想与著作和其他本土思想家在批判本土与新的生存模式上互补。在奥鲁卡看来，这些迹象表明：本土性并不像被广泛而错误地认为的那样，是思想上的匿名与停滞的同义词。

en: 5. What counts as Sage Philosophy?
zh: 5 什么算作智者哲学？

en: According to Oruka, Sage Philosophy is “the expressed thoughts of wise men and women in any given community and is a way of thinking and explaining the world that fluctuates between popular wisdom (well known communal maxims, aphorisms and general common sense truths) and didactic wisdom, an expounded wisdom and a rational thought of some given individuals within a community” (*Sage Philosophy*, p. 28). Oruka, however, had very definite ideas about who qualifies as a philosophic sage and how such persons are to be distinguished from other sages. When asked whether or not philosophy advances knowledge, Barasa is quoted as saying: “Yes. Being a rational method of inquiry into the real nature of things, philosophy is a means to re-examine knowledge and belief” (*Sage Philosophy*, p. 150). The tendency to express dissatisfaction with the status quo belief system of their communities is an important critical component and a criterion Oruka used to identify sages as philosophical. Dissatisfaction sometimes motivates the philosophic sage to advance the knowledge that everyone has by subjecting it to scrutiny in order to determine its validity and worth. While philosophic sages may still share with others some customary practices and beliefs, or aspects of them, unlike other members of their community, they emphasize rational explanations and justifications of courses of action. They owe greater loyalty to reason than to custom for its own sake. As a result, not only are sages often a source of new knowledge, but they are also a catalyst to change within their communities.
zh: 按奥鲁卡的说法，智者哲学是“任何给定共同体中有智慧的男男女女所表达的思想，是一种在大众智慧（众所周知的共同体格言、警句与一般常识真理）与教诲性智慧——一种被阐明的智慧与一个共同体中某些给定个体的理性思想——之间波动地思考与解释世界的方式”（*Sage Philosophy*, p. 28）。不过，奥鲁卡对谁有资格称为哲学智者、以及这样的人如何与其他智者区分，有非常明确的看法。当被问及哲学是否增进知识时，巴拉萨（Barasa）被引述说：“是的。作为一种对事物实在本性进行理性探究的方法，哲学是重新审查知识与信念的一种手段”（*Sage Philosophy*, p. 150）。表达对其共同体现状信念体系的不满的倾向，是奥鲁卡用来识别智者为哲学家的一个重要的批判性成分与判准。不满有时促使哲学智者把人人具有的知识置于审查之下以确定其有效性与价值，从而推进知识。哲学智者虽然可能仍与他人共享一些习俗实践与信念或其方面，但与其共同体的其他成员不同，他们强调对行动路线的理性解释与辩护。他们对理性的忠诚大于对习俗本身的忠诚。结果是：智者不仅是新知识的源泉，而且是其共同体内部变化的催化剂。

en: In the example cited above, Mbuya defines communalism in terms of a morality that appeals to the welfare of others as a guide to action. He indicates its goals, and limitations as a principle that aims at minimizing socio-economic disparity between the haves and the have-nots. On Oruka’s view, not every member of society carries out these kind of elaborations and conceptual clarifications of the principles that underlie what the majority live at the pragmatic level only as custom. While he recognizes that there are other indigenous sages in African communities, he distinguishes these from philosophic sages such as Mbuya and Chaungo, who are committed to critical inquiry and to the rational grounding of values and beliefs. Other indigenous sages, who may be wise in some sense, but not critically oriented, act as repositories of the statements of the beliefs of their communities, which they have learned and can repeat, or teach, to others exactly as they are supposed to be remembered.
zh: 在上面引的例子里，姆布亚以诉求于他人之福祉作为行动之向导的一种道德来定义公社主义。他指出了它的目标、以及它作为旨在最小化有产者与无产者之间社会经济差距的原则的限度。按奥鲁卡的看法，并非社会的每个成员都会对多数人在实践层面仅作为习俗来过活的那些原则，进行这类阐发与概念澄清。虽然他承认非洲共同体中还有其他本土智者，但他把这些人与致力于批判性探究、以及对价值与信念之理性奠基的哲学智者——如姆布亚与查翁戈——区分开来。其他可能在某种意义上聪明的本土智者，若不以批判为取向，则充当其共同体信念之陈述的储存者：他们学会了这些陈述、可以复述或教给他人，一如它们被要求被记住的样子。

en: This lattter group is exemplified by Ogotemmêli, a sage from the Dogon community in present-day Mali. His teachings were transcribed and commented on by the French philosopher and ethnographer Marcel Griaule in the now classic text, *Conversations with Ogotemmêli: Introduction to Dogon Religious Ideas* (Eng. tr. 1965), one of the outstanding texts of indigenous African thought. Ogotemmêli presents the commonly shared knowledge of the Dogon community, including not only their very complex theories about the origin of the universe and the subsequent development of material and non-material entities in it, but also a startling astronomical system that points to the Dogon’s pre-telescopic knowledge of the Sirius (A and B) and their paths across the skies. Yet, despite this pioneer scientific and mathematical genius, at no time throughout the entire presentation does one encounter Ogotemmêli as a thinker, only as the representative and narrator of the collective memory of his community. His own voice is submerged into a communal mode of expression. According to Oruka, the absence of any personal direct reflections on the issues at hand qualifies Ogotemmêli only as a folk sage. A folk sage is a highly intelligent and good narrator of traditionally imposed beliefs and myths. He, or she, may explain such beliefs and values with great detail and may even expound on the relation between the mythical representations and the lessons in and for society that they are intended to illustrate. But while the folk sage hardly veers off the narrative, by contrast, a philosophic sage is a person “of traditional African culture, capable of the critical, second-order type of thinking about the various problems of human life and nature; persons, that is, who subject beliefs that are traditionally taken for granted to independent rational reexamination and who are inclined to accept or reject such beliefs on the authority of reason rather than on the basis of a communal or religious consensus” (*Sage Philosophy*, pp. 5–6).
zh: 后一类人的例证是奥戈特默利（Ogotemmêli），来自今马里的多贡共同体的一位智者。他的教导由法国哲学家与民族志学家马塞尔·格里奥勒笔录并评论，成于如今已是经典文本的《与奥戈特默利对话：多贡宗教观念导论》（英译 1965）——本土非洲思想的杰出文本之一。奥戈特默利呈现的是多贡共同体的公共知识，不仅有他们关于宇宙起源及其中物质与非物质实体的后续发展的非常复杂的理论，还有一套令人惊讶的天文学系统，指向多贡人对天狼星（A 与 B）及其天空路径的前望远镜知识。然而，尽管有这种先驱性的科学与数学天才，在整篇呈现中，人们从未遇到作为思想者的奥戈特默利，只遇到作为其共同体集体记忆的代表与叙述者的他。他自己的声音被淹没在一种共同体的表达模式之中。按奥鲁卡的看法，任何个人的、直接的对所论问题的反思之缺席，只够把奥戈特默利算作民间智者。民间智者是传统所施加的信念与神话的极聪明、极好的叙述者。他或她可以极详尽地解释这类信念与价值，甚至可以阐发神话表象与它们意在说明的、社会之中与关乎社会的教训之间的关系。但民间智者几乎不离叙事；相比之下，哲学智者是“传统非洲文化中的人，能够对人类生活与自然的各种问题进行批判的、二阶的思想；也就是说，这样一些人：他们把传统上被视为理所当然的信念交付独立的理性再审，并且倾向于按理性的权威、而非按共同体或宗教共识的根据，来接受或拒绝这类信念”（*Sage Philosophy*, pp. 5–6）。

en: The onisegun, deliberately kept anonymous by Hallen and Sodipo for reasons of privacy, and who expound and elucidate the traditional thought of the Yoruba, are certainly wise and very knowledgeable people. On Oruka’s criteria for philosophic sagacity, however, they too are only folk sages. They are like Ogotemmêli, whose presentation, however complex and amazing in details, is exactly what every wise Dogon person is expected to know (*Sage Philosophy*, pp. 9–10). Oruka distinguishes between folk and philosophic sages, in terms of those who pursue the rational grounding of beliefs and values, as opposed to those who merely narrate them as they appear in their commuity’s belief systems.
zh: 由霍伦与索迪波出于隐私考虑刻意保持匿名的 onisegun——他们阐发与说明约鲁巴人的传统思想——当然是聪明的、极有学识的人。但按奥鲁卡关于哲学洞见的判准，他们同样只是民间智者。他们像奥戈特默利一样：其呈现无论多么复杂、细节多么惊人，恰恰是每一个聪明的多贡人都被期待知道的东西（*Sage Philosophy*, pp. 9–10）。奥鲁卡按追求信念与价值之理性奠基者、与只是按其在共同体信念体系中的样子叙述者，区分民间智者与哲学智者。

en: W. V. O. Quine’s indeterminacy thesis of radical translation presents a major difficulty for the explanations of the conceptual content and meaning of terms in Yoruba language provided by the onisegun to Hallen and Sodipo. Quine attacked the concept of universal propositions and meanings that are frequently assumed by translators to exist across all languages. This draws in question the practice of anthropologists studying African belief systems. Following Quine, Hallen argues that “Given the cumulative effects of the indeterminacy of translation between radically different languagaes, an alternative explanation for such inconsistencies could be that translators have recourse to contradiction because they, perhaps unwittingly, have not been able to arrive at a determinate or precise translation” (*A Short History of African Philosophy*, pp. 37–8). Failing to find in non-Western modes of thought precise translations of comparable rational expressions in their own languages, anthropologists hastened to conclude that the problem must lie with the non-Western modes of thought which appear to lack ways of accommodating rational expressions. Yet, Hallen and Sodipo’s own conversations with the Yoruba sages illustrate what happens when one tries to translate, among others, the English term “know” into Yoruba. The outcome of their comparative analyses shows that our conceptual assumptions about reality are often tied to the natural languages we speak. To be fair, Hallen’s and Sodipo’s work is not a simple description of what the onisegun said. Rather, they attempt to tease out what was intended conceptually in a language translated as faithfully as possible into propositions which they contrast with comparable ones in English. Nonetheless, Oruka maintained that any such use of Western philosophical language to analyze indigenous African thought leads to the separation “between an insider in traditional African philosophy and the outsider analyzing or describing this philosophy in a language of Western thought. Given this, the two cannot really meaningfully express their thought to each other and it would be absurd to find that one can be an expert in the thought of the other” (*Sage Philosophy*, p. 15).
zh: 蒯因（W. V. O. Quine）的彻底翻译的不确定性论题，给 onisegun 提供给霍伦与索迪波的、约鲁巴语中的概念内容与词项意义的说明，造成了重大困难。蒯因攻击了翻译者经常假定的普遍命题与普遍意义的观念——它们被假定为跨一切语言存在。这把研究非洲信念体系的人类学的实践拉入疑问。循蒯因，霍伦论证说：“鉴于在根本不同的语言之间翻译的不确定性的累积效应，这类不一致的另一种解释可能是：翻译者——也许在不知不觉中——未能达成一个确定的或精确的翻译”（*A Short History of African Philosophy*, pp. 37–8）。在非西方思想模式中找不到与其自身语言中可比的理性表达相对应的精确翻译，人类学家们就匆忙断定：问题必出在似乎缺乏容纳理性表达之方式的非西方思想模式上。然而，霍伦与索迪波自己与约鲁巴智者的对话表明：当人们尝试把英文词“know”等译入约鲁巴语时会发生什么。他们比较分析的成果表明：我们关于实在的概念假定常常与我们所说的自然语言绑在一起。平心而论，霍伦与索迪波的工作并不是对 onisegun 所说的东西的简单描述。毋宁说，他们试图梳理出在语言中被意图的概念内容，把它尽可能忠实地翻译成命题，并与英文中可比的命题相对照。尽管如此，奥鲁卡坚持：任何这类把西方哲学语言用于分析本土非洲思想的做法，都导致“传统非洲哲学的局内人与以西方思想的语言分析或描述这一哲学的局外人之间的分离。有鉴于此，二者无法真正有意义地向彼此表达其思想，而发现一个人可以是另一个人的思想的专家，将是荒谬的”（*Sage Philosophy*, p. 15）。

en: Conclusion
zh: 结论

en: It is not entirely clear what Oruka believed ought to be the relationship between the indigenous philosophic sage and his or her Western-trained counterpart. What is clear from his remarks is that the use of Western philosophers, like Quine or Wittgenstein, for example, as tools for analyzing the conceptual content of African modes of thought has allowed some scholars to champion “what they term ‘African philosophy’ by using terminology given in ‘Western philosophy’. None, so far, has given an account of what is to be treated as the language of African philosophy” (*Sage Philosophy*, p. 15). On this point at least, Oruka seems to position himself away from philosophers such as Appiah, Wiredu, and Gyekye. He understood the work of professional philosophers to be distinct from that of the philosophic sages and expressed the wish that they could remain so, as a way of preserving traditions. This idea appears to be implied by his regret that “The tragedy for man is that the Western intellectual elite has, over the years, successfully imposed its own culture and philosophy over the masses. So, British philosophy, for example, is taken to be the texts of Lockes, Humes, Bacons, Russels, etc.” (*Sage Philosophy*, p. 16). Oruka’s concern with the preservation of indigenous thought suggests that he desired to keep the professional school of philosophers separate from that of the philosophic sages to ensure the preservation of the intellectual integrity, not only of the sages, but of the African heritage as a whole. He was concerned that the language of African professional philosophers was too dependent on the Western conceptual lexicon and that its unchecked imposition on indigenous conceptual schemes might finally contribute to the demise of the latter.
zh: 奥鲁卡究竟认为本土的哲学智者与其受西方训练的同行之间应当是什么关系，并不完全清楚。从他的评论中清楚的是：使用蒯因或维特根斯坦之类的西方哲学家作为分析非洲思想模式之概念内容的工具，使得一些学者得以“通过使用‘西方哲学’给出的术语来提倡他们所谓的‘非洲哲学’。迄今没有人说明什么应当被当作非洲哲学的语言”（*Sage Philosophy*, p. 15）。至少在这一点上，奥鲁卡似乎把自己置于与阿皮亚、维雷杜与吉耶等哲学家不同的位置。他理解职业哲学家的工作与哲学智者的工作是有别的工作，并表达了对二者保持分别的希望，以此作为保存传统的方式。这一观念似乎隐含在他的遗憾之中：“人的悲剧在于，西方知识精英多年来成功地把他们自己的文化与哲学强加给大众。于是，举例说，英国哲学被当作洛克们、休谟们、培根们、罗素们等等的文本”（*Sage Philosophy*, p. 16）。奥鲁卡对保存本土思想的关注表明，他希望让职业哲学家的学派与哲学智者的学派保持分开，以确保——不仅是智者们的、而且是非洲遗产整体的——知识完整性的保存。他担心非洲职业哲学家的语言过分依赖西方的概念词库，而这种不加约束的强加于本土概念图式之上的做法，最终可能促成后者的消亡。

en: Among African philosophers, Kwasi Wiredu is particularly sympathetic to Oruka’s concerns. Writing on the need for conceptual decolonization in African philosophy, Wiredu claims that such a need would mean both “avoiding or reversing through a critical conceptual self-awareness the unexamined assimilation in our thought (that is, in the thought of contemporary African philosophers) of the conceptual frameworks embedded in the foreign philosophical traditions that have had impact on African life and thought…[and] exploiting as much as is judicious the resources of our own indigenous conceptual schemes in our philosophical meditations on even the most technical problems of contemporary philosophy” (*Cultural Universals and Particulars*, p. 136). At the same time, Wiredu agrees with other philosophers like Appiah and Gyekye in insisting that while the beliefs, proverbs, and customs of African cultures should be included in the philosophical reflections of the professional, such cultural elements of folk knowledge also must be subjected to critical analysis and evaluation because, “There is no pretense…that recourse to the African vernacular must result in instantaneous philosophic revelation” (*Cultural Universals and Particulars*, p. 138).
zh: 在非洲哲学家中，夸西·维雷杜对奥鲁卡的关切尤为同情。在论及非洲哲学中概念去殖民化之必要时，维雷杜主张，这一需要将同时意味着“通过批判性的概念自我觉知，避免或逆转我们（即当代非洲哲学家）思想中对嵌入于已影响非洲生活与思想的外来哲学传统中的概念框架的未经审查的吸纳……［以及］在我们对当代哲学甚至最技术性问题的哲学沉思中，尽可能地明智利用我们自己本土概念图式的资源”（*Cultural Universals and Particulars*, p. 136）。与此同时，维雷杜同意阿皮亚与吉耶等其他哲学家的看法，坚持：虽然非洲文化的信念、谚语与习俗应当被纳入职业哲学家的哲学反思之中，这些民间知识的文化要素也必须经受批判性的分析与评价，因为“没有任何伪装……说诉诸非洲本土语言就必定带来即时的哲学启示”（*Cultural Universals and Particulars*, p. 138）。

en: Oruka believed that professional African philosophers could interact with their sagacious counterparts, provided there was sufficient room for each to flourish separately. This idea suggests that he desired to expand the location of legitimate philosophical activity beyond the institutional confines of the academy, which he considered to be intricately connected to the colonial legacy. It is in this regard that the idea of African Sage philosophy has provided an important intervention in the development of contemporary African philosophy, addressing many crucial issues African philosophers continue to face in the wider context of postcolonial cultural inquiry, of which philosophy is only a part. Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak in *A Critique of Postcolonial Reason: Toward a History of a Vanishing Present* (1999) has suggested that the self-awareness stage in postcolonial theory is largely over and that the formerly colonized cultures are settling down to utilizing their respective cultural reservoirs without significant attention to the need to reclaim their indigenous voices, and without minimizing the need for a continued and sustained awareness of the ever-present Eurocentric impositions. This orientation is displayed, for example, in Wiredu’s independent, but comparative, analyses of Western and African concepts, whose widely-debated epistemological position that “truth is nothing but opinion,” hinges on the contrast between the objectivist implications of the claim “I know that” in English and the non-objectivist implications in the Akan language.
zh: 奥鲁卡相信，职业非洲哲学家可以与其睿智的同行互动，只要有足够的余地让各自分别繁荣。这一观念表明，他希望把正当哲学活动的场所扩展到学院的组织界限之外——他认为后者与殖民遗产纠结相连。正是在这个方面，非洲智者哲学的观念为当代非洲哲学的发展提供了一个重要的介入，处理非洲哲学家在后殖民文化探究——哲学只是其中一部分——的更广语境中持续面对的许多关键问题。佳亚特里·斯皮瓦克（Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak）在《后殖民理性批判：通向正在消失的当下的历史》（1999）中提出：后殖民理论中的自我觉知阶段大体已经过去，先前被殖民的文化正在安定下来利用其各自的文化储备，而无须显著地关注收回其本土声音的必要，也无须淡化对始终在场的欧洲中心强加的持续而持续的觉知。这种取向例如显示于维雷杜对西方与非洲概念的独立的、但比较性的分析之中——他那被广泛争论的认识论立场“真理不外乎意见”，关键在于英文断言“我知道那个”的客观主义意味与阿肯语中的非客观主义意味之间的对照。

en: Along with Wiredu, Hallen and Sodipo also hold that very complex philosophical views are already signaled by many sayings in African languages, and wait to be teased out through careful analysis and interpretation. Although Oruka’s idea of the sages as philosophically savvy in their own languages raises methodical questions as to whether sage philosophy is the property of the professional philosopher, or of the indigenous wise person, and only teased out through the prompting of a professional philosopher, Hallen, Sodipo and Wiredu agree with his insistence that the distinguishing marks of African philosophy emerge precisely out of analytical involvement by Western-trained philosophers, who raise questions regarding the conceptual underpinnings of indigenous beliefs, values, and languages, and critically examine their meaning and implications. They propose, on this basis, to accommodate both indigenous sages, and Western-trained professionals, as philosophers.
zh: 与维雷杜一道，霍伦与索迪波也主张：许多非洲语言中的谚语已经标示出非常复杂的哲学观点，等着通过仔细的分析与解释被梳理出来。虽然奥鲁卡“智者在自己的语言中即具哲学头脑”的观念，提出了智者哲学是职业哲学家的财产、还是本土智者的财产、只是借职业哲学家的提示才被梳理出来这样的方法论问题，霍伦、索迪波与维雷杜同意他的坚持：非洲哲学的区辨性标记恰恰出自受西方训练的哲学家的分析性介入——他们提出关于本土信念、价值与语言的概念根基的问题，并批判地审查其意义与意蕴。他们在此基础上提出，把本土智者与受西方训练的职业人士都容纳为哲学家。
